a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On Africa's dependency on foreign aid: "There is no form of bondage more degrading than dependency – living on subsidies and hand-outs. To rely on aid instead of working, producing, and utilizing one's resources to achieve a higher standard of living is, in effect, a modern form of slavery." Said Trump's aid cuts "can be considered as a blessing in disguise which will impel a quest for other alternatives – that will push Africa to think differently, to seek new solutions, and to build internal systems of support." Said aid distribution "has become a business" for NGOs, making it harder to dismantle dependency.

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On US-Eritrea relations under Trump: Said "Since 1991, Eritrea has pursued a policy of constructive engagement. Not in the hope of securing subsidies, handouts, or protection from them, but rather in the belief that past mistakes should be corrected and that new constructive relationships can be built." Said Eritrea's plan is "to resume engagement with the Trump administration starting from 2026 up to 2028," noting three years under Trump's first term and four years under Biden were effectively lost to sanctions and hostility.

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On timing of re-engagement: Said "we consider 2025 as a year for laying the groundwork," and that Eritrea "will finalize our preparations this year and vigorously pursue our policy of constructive engagement in the subsequent three years." Dismissed as "misleading narratives" claims that Washington backs Ethiopia's quest for maritime access.

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On Ethiopian accusations that Eritrea is preparing for war: "These statements are infantile and difficult to fathom; one wouldn't expect even a child to speak in such a way. Fabricating and spreading cheap lies is both disgusting and unbecoming." Called Ethiopia's complaint to the UN Secretary-General "a duplicitous and shameful act designed to cover-up the actual declared war," and urged Ethiopia to "desist from these diversionary ploys and focus on resolving their own internal problems."

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On Ethiopian sea-access ambitions: Described being told by the Ethiopian government "that Djibouti makes 3 to 4 billion dollars; and that we could take half, or even all of the revenue," which he called "a moral taboo to us." Said claims of naval-base and port-control ambitions from the Suez Canal to Dar es Salaam "can only originate from an audacious mindset," and blamed the UAE president specifically for bankrolling such schemes.

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On accusations of Eritrean warmongering: "We have no interest, whatsoever, in waging war... Eritrea and its people abhor war. But, when and if war is brought to our doorsteps, we know how to defend ourselves." Said "Those who accuse Eritrea of warmongering or of harboring ambitions of military aggression are either ignorant of history or deliberately misrepresenting it. Such allegations are not only unfounded but infantile."

a43.speaker: President Isaias Afwerki, President of Eritrea
a43.name: President Isaias Afwerki
a43.title: President of Eritrea
a43.speech: On regional integration: "Fostering integration at the regional and wider neighbourhood levels remains a matter that we continuously strive for through political goodwill and sound policies." Said IGAD and the African Union have failed in practice but this is "not a reason for despair," and concluded "Integration is an irreplaceable choice."

a225.speaker: House of Representatives of Nigeria
a225.name: House of Representatives of Nigeria
a225.speech: Has resolved to probe the management of over $4.6 billion in international health grants received by Nigeria from the Global Fund and the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) between 2021 and 2025; following extensive debate, the House directed its Committee on HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Control to investigate the disbursement and use of funds received from the Global Fund and USAID between 2021 and 2025, with findings expected within four weeks for further legislative action.

a225.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, member of the House of Representatives
a225.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a225.title: member of the House of Representatives
a225.speech: Moved a motion on Tuesday expressing concern over the lack of transparency and accountability in the handling of these funds, despite Nigeria's persistent struggle with preventable diseases ; lamented that Nigeria still ranks among countries with the highest burdens of malaria, HIV/AIDS, and TB worldwide, questioned the impact of these interventions and stressed the need for enhanced legislative oversight to ensure value for money.

a225.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, member of the House of Representatives
a225.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a225.title: member of the House of Representatives
a225.speech: According to the lawmaker, Nigeria received approximately $1.8 billion from the Global Fund between 2021 and 2024 to strengthen disease control initiatives and implement the Resilient and Sustainable Systems for Health (RSSH) project; he explained that the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM-Nigeria) is the institution responsible for implementing Global Fund programmes, while the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare manages USAID-supported initiatives ; further revealed that USAID provided more than $2.8 billion in grants within the same period for HIV/AIDS, TB, malaria, and other community health programmes, and highlighted that through PEPFAR, the U.S. government has contributed over $6 billion to Nigeria's HIV/AIDS response since inception.

a225.speaker: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah, member of the House of Representatives
a225.name: Hon. Amobi Godwin Ogah
a225.title: member of the House of Representatives
a225.speech: Expressed dismay that Nigeria continues to record alarming health statistics, citing data that shows 51,000 AIDS-related deaths were recorded in 2023, including 15,000 children under 14 years old; added that the country accounts for 26.6 percent of global malaria cases and 31 percent of malaria deaths, while ranking first in Africa and sixth globally for TB, representing 4.6 percent of the worldwide burden. "These figures are troubling. Despite the billions of dollars in international aid, Nigeria continues to lose lives to diseases that are preventable. It is imperative that we evaluate how these funds are being utilized," Ogah stated.

a225.speaker: Lawmakers (House of Representatives)
a225.name: Lawmakers (House of Representatives)
a225.speech: Maintained that proper oversight of foreign health grants is crucial to ensuring that such funds achieve their intended purpose and help Nigeria meet the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) target of eliminating HIV, TB, and malaria by 2030.

Our vision is to fight hunger and reach a stage where emaSwati are able to feed themselves, instead of relying on imports. That is the ultimate measure of food sovereignty."

a756.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister for Agriculture of Eswatini

a756.speaker: Mandla Tshawuka, Minister for Agriculture of Eswatini

This project is central to our national food security goals." He said these initiatives, together with SAPEMP and a World Bank-funded youth empowerment project, collectively form the backbone of the country's push towards food sovereignty and rural economic transformation.

a914.name: Sylvia Ekra

a914.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)

a1064.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.name: H.E. Retieb Kamel
a1064.title: new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.speech: Delivered a speech paying vibrant tribute to the martyrs of the 1 November 1954 Revolution and taking stock of the cooperation between his country and Mali. He explained that in triggering this glorious Revolution the National Liberation Front (FLN) was not placing its struggle solely in the quest for national independence against the French colonial regime, but wanted above all to be a symbol of defiance and self-determination for oppressed nations throughout the world; that the Revolution subsequently inspired numerous revolutionary movements across Africa, Asia and Latin America; that "the Algerian Revolution was not only crucial for its own people, but also served as a model for anti-colonial movements the world over", and that Algeria's success encouraged other nations, from Angola to South Africa, to challenge the colonial powers and assert their sovereignty.

a1064.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.name: H.E. Retieb Kamel
a1064.title: new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.speech: Said that in the field of bilateral cooperation his country continues to affirm its leadership role in North Africa by actively engaging in regional diplomacy and the promotion of peace and stability; that Algeria, under the presidency of Abdelmadjid Tebboune, continues to favour constructive diplomacy and promotes solidarity within the Arab, African and Mediterranean communities; and that as a key member of the African Union and of the Non-Aligned Movement, Algeria remains a fervent defender of the right of nations to govern themselves without outside interference.

a1064.speaker: H.E. Retieb Kamel, new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.name: H.E. Retieb Kamel
a1064.title: new Ambassador of Algeria to Mali
a1064.speech: On Mali, he said that, grateful for the active solidarity Algeria received from its partners during the years of struggle for independence, foremost among them Mali, independent Algeria has striven to develop good-neighbourly relations with all the countries with which it shares borders. Besides the annual offer of scholarships, of which 270 for Mali for the 2024-2025 academic year, making it the leading beneficiary of Algerian government scholarships worldwide, Algeria has always been present in difficult times and in situations of natural disaster, providing support and diversified humanitarian aid: "Military and intelligence cooperation has not been left out of this effort, Algeria having provided Mali with multifaceted technical support; transfers of various military materials and equipment; and military training at all levels, in the various institutes, specialised higher schools, the Staff College and the Cherchell school." He added that Algeria, favouring the mixing of populations with African countries, has agreed with seven of them, including Mali, not to place barriers on the free movement of persons and not to impose a visa requirement.

a1206.speaker: Internal State Department document (recommendations by its undersecretary for management)
a1206.name: Internal State Department document (recommendations by its undersecretary for management)
a1206.speech: The United States government is weighing at closing nearly 30 overseas embassies and consulates including in South Sudan, according to an internal State Department document. The internal document also recommends reducing the footprint at the US diplomatic missions in Somalia and Iraq where the US is engaged in counterterrorism efforts, and resizing other diplomatic outposts. Posts identified for closure include embassies in Malta, Luxembourg, Lesotho, the Republic of Congo, the Central African Republic and South Sudan, as well as consulates in France, Germany, Bosnia and Herzegovina, the United Kingdom, South Africa and South Korea. The document recommends closing 10 embassies and 17 consulates mainly in Europe and Africa, as well as the Caribbean and Asia. The document proposes that the closed embassies' duties be covered by outposts in neighboring countries.

a1631.name: Tom Kaydor
a1631.title: Jr., Assistant Professor at the IBB Graduate School of International Studies, University of Liberia (opinion columnist)
a1631.speech: Criticised the free tuition policy, saying former President George Weah "without consultation with the Board and Administration made that tuition free policy pronouncement abruptly," and argued this Government must refine the policy, asking whether public school students should attend tuition-free higher education without any responsibility to the State and proposing a National Service requirement after graduation.

a1715.speaker: Evelyn Chisambiro, visual artist and proprietor of Kaliso Art Gallery in Lilongwe
a1715.name: Evelyn Chisambiro
a1715.title: visual artist and proprietor of Kaliso Art Gallery in Lilongwe
a1715.speech: Said on Monday that economic challenges that Malawians are going through at the moment have not spared the creative sector, and that due to low buying power among Malawians, artworks were not selling as hot cakes. "To make matters worse, artworks are regarded as a luxury among some people." ; "People are holding on to their money to buy necessities, such that they do not have disposable income for artworks." ; "We cannot hike prices for artworks despite investing more in them because, somehow, some people regard them as a luxury."

a1715.speaker: Evelyn Chisambiro, visual artist and proprietor of Kaliso Art Gallery in Lilongwe
a1715.name: Evelyn Chisambiro
a1715.title: visual artist and proprietor of Kaliso Art Gallery in Lilongwe
a1715.speech: Said there was a need for visual artists and the creative sector as a whole to keep having conversations in order to find markets for high value products, and was quick to say that art can bring about solutions to problems: "We need to look at how we can be exporting art to make money with which to make ends meet. There is talent in Malawi."

a1783.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine (post on X)
a1783.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
a1783.title: President of Ukraine (post on X)
a1783.speech: Accused Russia of launching a record number of strike drones: “Last night, Russia attacked Ukraine, launching a record number of strike drones —188 — against our people. I want to thank our defenders of the sky for repelling the attack.” ; “Around 80 drones were shot down, and more than 90 were lost due to location disruption.” ; “Unfortunately, there has been damage to our critical infrastructure, and the situation in Ternopil remains challenging.” ; “All services and repair crews are on-site, doing everything to assist people and restore electricity as quickly as possible.”

a1783.speaker: Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine (post on X)
a1783.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
a1783.title: President of Ukraine (post on X)
a1783.speech: Noted that each drone contained 85 foreign-made components, nearly 16,000 in total: “188 drones. Each contains 85 foreign-made components—nearly 16,000 in total, without which they could not be launched. These attacks are possible only because of Russia’s ability to circumvent sanctions through various schemes.” ; “We thank everyone worldwide who blocks such supplies, but we need greater collective efforts to enforce sanctions and force Russia to stop this war. We must put an end to Russian aggression.” ; “If you are against the war, you must truly be against Russia’s circumvention of sanctions.”

a2157.speaker: Resolution of the Council of Ministers no. 103/2024 of 18 November (State of Cabo Verde)
a2157.name: Resolution of the Council of Ministers no. 103/2024 of 18 November (State of Cabo Verde)
a2157.speech: The State of Cabo Verde "declares terminated the Establishment Convention and its respective Addendum concluded between the State of Cabo Verde and the companies MLD Cabo Verde Resort SA and MLD Cabo Verde Entretenimento SA, as well as the Concession Contracts for Ilheu Santa Maria and the wet surface and the concession for the Operation of Games of Chance, and the consequent reversion of the assets transferred or built by MLD under the Investment Project (PI) in the said areas."

a2157.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2157.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a2157.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2157.speech: Paints the portrait of a country that is now more resilient after being tested by the Covid-19 pandemic and by the inflation crisis caused by the war in Ukraine; considers that the country knew how to face these crises, highlighting the economic growth recorded over the last two post-pandemic years: "We have a more resilient country that has been put fully to the test" ; "But it is not only economic growth. It is economic growth with a reduction in unemployment, a reduction in the poverty rate, accompanied by inclusive and active policies of employability and of social inclusion and protection, which shows that we have managed to face difficult situations; we have managed to recover, we are relaunching the economy and there is a positive feeling of confidence, not only externally but also within Cabo Verde" ; says he expects from this state of the Nation debate a clarifying discussion, with less friction and with the presentation of political alternatives by the opposition.

a2157.speaker: Eugenio Moeda, Pro-Capital
a2157.name: Eugenio Moeda
a2157.title: Pro-Capital
a2157.speech: "We have an investment portfolio of 180 thousand contos."

a2157.speaker: Bestfly (airline currently operating domestic flights)
a2157.name: Bestfly (airline currently operating domestic flights)
a2157.speech: Guarantees that it will continue in Cabo Verde.

a2157.speaker: Ligia Dias Fonseca, lawyer and former First Lady
a2157.name: Ligia Dias Fonseca
a2157.title: lawyer and former First Lady
a2157.speech: "Our humanity lies in what we were, in what we are and in our ethical values" ; in an interview reviewing 2023 she shares her personal view of the year, reflects on the present and looks ahead to the coming year, and calls for a strong investment in education, covering technological knowledge but also history and philosophy, creating the ethical foundations for making the right decisions in a challenging future.

a2157.speaker: Government of Cabo Verde
a2157.name: Government of Cabo Verde
a2157.speech: Clarified today that Jorge Benchimol Duarte, now chairman of the Executive Committee of Cabo Verde Airports, was not part of the negotiating team on the side of the State of Cabo Verde during the concession negotiations.

a2157.speaker: Commission monitoring the airport concession process
a2157.name: Commission monitoring the airport concession process
a2157.speech: According to the commission, the Vinci group has until 18 July to fulfil the 21 conditions of the concession contract for the management of the national airports and aerodromes signed a year ago with the State.

a2157.speaker: Explanatory note accompanying the draft law classifying Portuguese as cultural heritage
a2157.name: Explanatory note accompanying the draft law classifying Portuguese as cultural heritage
a2157.speech: Begins by presenting the Portuguese language as an integral and structuring part of Cabo Verdean history, society and identity and then concludes that one cannot remain "indifferent to signs of fatigue" in its use, which run counter to the value it should be given as a language of internal communication and as the international language of the State of Cabo Verde.

a2157.speaker: Joao Lima, President of the Association of Fishing Shipowners of Cabo Verde (APESC)
a2157.name: Joao Lima
a2157.title: President of the Association of Fishing Shipowners of Cabo Verde (APESC)
a2157.speech: "At this moment, the shipowner is just trying to survive" ; says the fisheries sector is one to which politicians do not give due attention.

a2157.speaker: Antonio Costa, Prime Minister of Portugal
a2157.name: Antonio Costa
a2157.title: Prime Minister of Portugal
a2157.speech: Announced his country's willingness to take part in the fund being created by Cabo Verde.

a2157.speaker: Directorate General of Heritage and Public Procurement (DGPCP) (statement)
a2157.name: Directorate General of Heritage and Public Procurement (DGPCP) (statement)
a2157.speech: Guaranteed on Tuesday, through a statement, that the accusation by the Praia Municipal Council that there are two purchase and sale contracts for the land where the new Varzea secondary school is being built is not true; it reaffirms that the contract is valid and remains valid, on its proper terms.

a2157.speaker: Banco de Cabo Verde (BCV)
a2157.name: Banco de Cabo Verde (BCV)
a2157.speech: Decided to expand the collateral for monetary financing operations (OMF), in a context of uncertainty caused by the new Covid-19 Omicron variant.

a2226.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.name: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.speech: Declared, as quoted by the news agency France-Presse (AFP): "The situation in the Gaza Strip is increasingly worrying and painful," launching an appeal for the entry of "decent humanitarian aid" into Gaza at his first weekly general audience in St Peter's Square since his election on 8 May.

a2226.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.name: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.speech: On 11 May had already said he was "deeply saddened" by what was happening in the Gaza Strip and called at the time for "an immediate cessation of hostilities, humanitarian aid for the exhausted civilian population and the release of all the hostages."

a2226.speaker: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.name: Pope Leo XIV
a2226.speech: Argued before more than 25,000 faithful at the general audience that it is necessary to work for peace in a world at war: "In a world divided by hatred and war, we are called to sow hope and to build peace," as also quoted by the Spanish news agency EFE ; during the greeting to Portuguese-speaking faithful, invited them to pray the rosary for peace: "In this Marian month, I would like to reiterate the invitation of Our Lady of Fatima: 'Pray the rosary every day for peace.' Together with Mary, we ask that men do not close themselves to this gift of God and that they disarm their hearts."

a2226.speaker: Israeli authorities
a2226.name: Israeli authorities
a2226.speech: Announced on Tuesday that they had allowed some trucks with baby food into Gaza, and say that around a hundred trucks of aid have been allowed into the Gaza Strip since Monday.

a2226.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2226.name: World Health Organization (WHO)
a2226.speech: Denounced that two million Palestinians were going hungry.

a2226.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2226.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
a2226.speech: Accused Israel of only allowing into Gaza aid that is "ridiculously insufficient" so as not to be accused of "starving the population to death," said the aid authorised into the Gaza Strip "is nothing but a smokescreen," and denounced that the siege Israel imposed on Gaza at the beginning of March, to force the Palestinian extremist group Hamas to release the hostages it still holds, is being maintained.

a2226.speaker: Italian Government (statement)
a2226.name: Italian Government (statement)
a2226.speech: Reported in a communiqué that, hours before the audience, Leo XIV had confirmed to the Italian Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, the Vatican's readiness to host negotiations between Ukraine and Russia.

a2353.speaker: Baroness Scotland, Commonwealth Secretary-General (Informal Assessment Report)
a2353.name: Baroness Scotland
a2353.title: Commonwealth Secretary-General (Informal Assessment Report)
a2353.speech: Has recommended the country be allowed to return more than 20 years after its expulsion; her Informal Assessment Report says that "stakeholders" in Zimbabwe have "reported an overall improved political environment", adding: "I am certain that with the help of the Commonwealth family the country will flourish once again."

a2353.speaker: Baroness Scotland, Commonwealth Secretary-General
a2353.name: Baroness Scotland
a2353.title: Commonwealth Secretary-General
a2353.speech: Says that while the country was "still in the early stages of its democratic journey and challenges remain, including the issue of political prisoners and upholding freedom of association, most of the core criteria have been sufficiently and broadly met", and recommends Zimbabwe membership progresses to the "next stage", which entails her consultation with member countries.

a2353.speaker: Africa Confidential
a2353.name: Africa Confidential
a2353.speech: Says she made the recommendation despite criticism of Zimbabwe 2023 elections in a Commonwealth Observers Report which has been slow to emerge.

a2353.speaker: Commonwealth Observers Report
a2353.name: Commonwealth Observers Report
a2353.speech: Found "shortcomings with the process that call into question the credibility, transparency and inclusivity of the election" and added that Zimbabwe had passed laws that "negatively impacted journalistic freedoms."

a2353.speaker: Commonwealth spokesman
a2353.name: Commonwealth spokesman
a2353.speech: Said: "We have ascertained that all stakeholders (government, opposition, civil society, media, religious leaders etc) are eager to see Zimbabwe back in the family."

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué), chaired by President Alassane Ouattara
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.title: chaired by President Alassane Ouattara
a2384.speech: Adopted a draft law on the fight against climate change, stating that climate change has significantly affected the country in recent years, disturbing the ecological balance and socio-economic life with serious and growing threats to the well-being and health of the population, and that the law aims to strengthen existing arrangements for adaptation and mitigation in line with the country’s international commitments.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted an ordinance amending articles 3 and 17 of ordinance no. 2017-500 of 2 August 2017 on electronic exchanges, stating that it falls within the implementation of the “National Cybersecurity Strategy 2021-2025” and entrusts the fight against cybercrime and the protection of computer systems to a single dedicated structure ; Adopted a decree creating the National Agency for Information Systems Security (ANSSI), the new national body dedicated to cybersecurity, concentrating all powers formerly vested in the various structures for combating cybercrime.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted two decrees on the powers, composition, organisation and functioning of the Reform Commission and of the Administrative Appeals Commission, stating that they reorganise these advisory bodies so as to improve the effectiveness and professionalism of the Public Service and to promote a higher sense of responsibility in public services.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted a decree dissolving pupils’ and students’ associations of a trade-union character, stating that such associations repeatedly engage in serious excesses, that an operation to clean up university residences uncovered numerous bladed weapons used to commit crimes and sow disorder on campuses, and that the measure aims to preserve public order and security and durably guarantee calm and social cohesion in school and university spaces.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted a decree approving the “Kong Solaire” concession agreement for a 50 MWp solar plant in the Tchologo region at Kong, signed in July 2024, providing for annual production of 92,304.36 MWh, a performance ratio of 84.44% and an annual availability rate of 99%, for an overall cost of 37.45 billion CFA francs ; Adopted two decrees granting mining exploration permits to YESSATI GOLD RESOURCES SARL (gold, Abengourou) and IVOIRE GOLD SARL/IVOGOLD SARL (nickel, rare earths, cobalt, gold and chromium, Ouangolodougou), valid for four years.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted a decree creating the National Platform on Sustainable Finance, stating that it is issued in application of the Resilience and Sustainability Facility agreement concluded in March 2024 with the IMF, in order to accelerate major structural reforms in climate policy, and that the Platform is responsible for coordinating green and sustainable financing.

a2384.speaker: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.name: Council of Ministers of Côte d’Ivoire (communiqué)
a2384.speech: Adopted four decrees on the National Centre for Arts and Culture (CNAC), the National Commission for the Francophonie (CNF), the Ivorian Office of Cultural Heritage (OIPC) and the Bernard Binlin-Dadié Palace of Culture (PCBD), stating that they bring these structures into line with the reform carried by law no. 2020-627 of 14 August 2020 on national public establishments.

a2384.speaker: Prime Minister, Head of Government, Minister of Sports and the Living Environment (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.name: Prime Minister
a2384.title: Head of Government, Minister of Sports and the Living Environment (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.speech: Reported on the implementation of the Government’s Social Programme (PSGouv) as at the end of September 2024, stating that significant progress was recorded in several sectors, including 708,606 children vaccinated free of charge against penta 3 and 681,756 against measles/rubella, 364,017 pregnant women receiving free delivery kits, 74,687 young people placed in programmes, 205,000 households receiving a quarterly social safety-net allowance and 396 localities electrified, with an overall commitment rate of 67.18% (792.7 billion CFA francs) and a disbursement rate of 66.88% (789.1 billion CFA francs).

a2384.speaker: Ministry of State, Ministry of the Public Service and Modernisation of the Administration (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.name: Ministry of State
a2384.title: Ministry of the Public Service and Modernisation of the Administration (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.speech: Reported on the 2023 electronic attendance-monitoring operation, stating that it covered a target population of 251,426 civil servants and State agents, that 249,549 agents were confirmed present at their post and 1,877 were absent or not checked, and that those agents were subject to immediate measures including suspension of pay and may still refer their case to the Disciplinary Board.

a2384.speaker: Ministry of State, Ministry of the Public Service and Modernisation of the Administration (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.name: Ministry of State
a2384.title: Ministry of the Public Service and Modernisation of the Administration (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.speech: Reported on the strike observed by certain health and education/training trade unions from 15 to 17 October 2024, stating that it was launched despite negotiations opened by the Government and the legal forms prescribed by law no. 92-571 of 11 September 1992, that preventive measures minimised its disruptive effects, that the twenty-six principal ringleaders had their salaries suspended and other participants had three days’ pay deducted, and that disciplinary proceedings would be initiated against the leaders of this illegal strike from the following week, without prejudice to criminal proceedings before the Public Prosecutor.

a2384.speaker: Ministry of the Economy, Planning and Development (report to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.name: Ministry of the Economy
a2384.title: Planning and Development (report to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.speech: Reported on Côte d’Ivoire’s participation in the Annual Meetings of the World Bank Group and the IMF held from 21 to 26 October 2024, stating that the meetings highlighted the resilience of the world economy and Africa’s positioning in Bretton Woods reforms with the creation of a third chair on the IMF Board of Directors, that the IMF, the World Bank Group and private sector actors welcomed the significant progress recorded by the country, and that the mission was marked by the signing of two financing agreements, one with the OPEC Fund for 39.3 billion CFA francs and the other of 2.7 billion CFA francs with the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC).

a2384.speaker: Ministry for the Promotion of Youth, Professional Integration and Civic Service (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.name: Ministry for the Promotion of Youth
a2384.title: Professional Integration and Civic Service (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a2384.speech: Reported on the state of progress of PEJEDEC 3 as at 30 September 2024, stating that the project targets 102,000 direct and more than 300,000 indirect beneficiaries for 86.7 billion CFA francs, that 41,882 beneficiaries had been registered (an achievement rate of 81.64%), that 68,000 young beneficiaries were registered under the decentralisation component and 5,120 young people taken in charge under the training-employment transition component, with 43.2 billion CFA francs disbursed, a rate of 49.9%.

a2384.speaker: National Commission for the Fight against Climate Change (CNLCC), annual report adopted by the Council of Ministers
a2384.name: National Commission for the Fight against Climate Change (CNLCC)
a2384.title: annual report adopted by the Council of Ministers
a2384.speech: Presents the state of implementation of the Nationally Determined Contributions and the growing harmful impacts of climate change on the environment, the economy and communities over the period from the adoption of the Paris Agreement to September 2024, and emphasises the Government’s efforts through the adoption of policies and strategies, capacity building, the development of resilient infrastructure and the promotion of renewable energies, with around 270 projects implemented, 90 in Adaptation and 180 in Mitigation.

a2384.speaker: Amadou Coulibaly, Minister of Communication, Government Spokesperson (issuer of the communiqué)
a2384.name: Amadou Coulibaly
a2384.title: Minister of Communication, Government Spokesperson (issuer of the communiqué)
a2384.speech: Announced under ‘Miscellaneous’ that, within the framework of COP 29, the Vice-President of the Republic will travel from 10 to 15 November 2024 to Baku, in Azerbaijan, and that the next Council of Ministers will be held on Wednesday 20 November 2024 in Abidjan.

a2446.speaker: Asim Alamin, manager, CTC Group plant in Bahri
a2446.name: Asim Alamin
a2446.title: manager, CTC Group plant in Bahri
a2446.speech: “This factory made electrical products with all the components,” ; “Now we are rehabilitating it. Hopefully we will return to what it was before.”

a2446.speaker: World Bank data
a2446.name: World Bank data
a2446.speech: Sudan's GDP contracted 29% the year the war started and 13.5% in 2024.

a2446.speaker: United Nations
a2446.name: United Nations
a2446.speech: More than one million people have returned to Khartoum.

a2446.speaker: CTC Group (statement to Reuters)
a2446.name: CTC Group (statement to Reuters)
a2446.speech: “Our manufacturing complex suffered heavy damage – buildings, electrical systems and vital equipment were looted or destroyed” ; “Before the end of this year, we expect to see our production lines running once more.”

a2446.speaker: Moawia Elbereir, head of Sudan's business union
a2446.name: Moawia Elbereir
a2446.title: head of Sudan's business union
a2446.speech: “Right now, the number of factories that have returned to work is relatively small,” put the losses for the industrial sector at $50 billion ; “The biggest obstacle to restarting the rest of the industrial areas is electricity, fuel prices and new fees levied on us.”

a2446.speaker: Safaa Adam, factory worker
a2446.name: Safaa Adam
a2446.title: factory worker
a2446.speech: Said she and her family were left penniless after the war started: “We lived in circumstances we would have never imagined. We ate expired food, and sometimes couldn't find that” ; “Once again I have a steady income.”

a2488.speaker: IHS 2016 (Integrated Household Survey, cited data)
a2488.name: IHS 2016 (Integrated Household Survey
a2488.title: cited data)
a2488.speech: Cited as the source for the finding that the Agricultural Sector's contribution to GDP declined to 20% in 2016 (from 31%).

a2488.speaker: Maputo African Union Agreement
a2488.name: Maputo African Union Agreement
a2488.speech: Provides that countries provide 10% of their National Budgets to the Agricultural Sector.

a2488.speaker: NADA Act, 2006 (Gambian legislation)
a2488.name: NADA Act
a2488.title: 2006 (Gambian legislation)
a2488.speech: Enacted by Parliament in 2006 establishing a National Agricultural Development Agency (NADA), put together by the PMO and MDI.

a2652.speaker: Benvinda Levi, Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.name: Benvinda Levi
a2652.title: Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.speech: Says that the new international situation imposed by the United States of America forces countries to consolidate bilateral trade. Stressed that the current situation in international trade imposed by the United States obliges countries to consolidate trade relations at the bilateral level. “The recent decision by the United States forces countries to think about how to maximise bilateral trade and take advantage of the comparative advantages that countries have in particular,” she underlined.

a2652.speaker: Benvinda Levi, Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.name: Benvinda Levi
a2652.title: Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.speech: Said that, in order to consolidate these relations, Colombian businesspeople accompanying the Vice-President had been at FACIM to identify areas of investment. “In the field of investment, we would like to note that the delegation of Her Excellency the Vice-President of Colombia is accompanied by businesspeople who are taking the opportunity to be at FACIM, to see the potential the country offers and, from there, to see to what extent we can cooperate and boost our trade relations.” ; Said that the parties will continue to work in multilateral forums of which both are part, such as the United Nations, the Non-Aligned Movement and the Group of 77 plus China, as well as other multilateral organisations such as the World Trade Organization. ; Said that this meeting serves as a path towards establishing relations in several other areas, with particular emphasis on the economic one.

a2652.speaker: Benvinda Levi, Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.name: Benvinda Levi
a2652.title: Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.speech: “We spoke about the possibility of developing air communications in the future, that is, air transport between Mozambique and Colombia, in order to allow a better strengthening of relations between the two countries,” she stressed.

a2652.speaker: Francia Mina (Francia Márquez), Vice-President of Colombia
a2652.name: Francia Mina (Francia Márquez)
a2652.title: Vice-President of Colombia
a2652.speech: Thanked the Prime Minister for the invitation to visit Mozambique extended to Colombia last year and also invited the country to take part in the Agrarian Summit in Colombia next year. “Likewise, the Agrarian Summit is scheduled to take place in Colombia next year, and Mozambique has been invited to participate in this Agrarian Summit.” For the stateswoman, the summit will be fertile ground for exchange and sharing of experiences, commitment to food sovereignty and the eradication of hunger in the world.

a2652.speaker: Benvinda Levi, Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.name: Benvinda Levi
a2652.title: Prime Minister of Mozambique
a2652.speech: The parties described the meeting as very productive and of great importance for strengthening the historic relations between the two countries. Benvinda Levi said the talks were very useful and fruitful, “in which we shared our points of view quite openly on various matters of common interest.”

a2724.speaker: President Nangolo Mbumba of Namibia
a2724.name: President Nangolo Mbumba of Namibia
a2724.speech: says the noble gesture of humanitarian assistance from Qatar is testimony to the strong bonds of friendship and growing relations between the two countries.

a2915.speaker: Prof Makame Mbarawa, Tanzania’s Minister for Transport
a2915.name: Prof Makame Mbarawa
a2915.title: Tanzania’s Minister for Transport
a2915.speech: Said that the rehabilitation of TAZARA will bring significant benefits, including enhanced cargo transportation from the Port of Dar es Salaam to Zambia and other SADC member states, and that the improvements will reduce transport costs and time, stimulate regional trade, attract investment, increase employment and income for citizens and strengthen diplomatic and economic ties between Tanzania, Zambia and China ; extended his gratitude to the three governments for their solidarity and commitment to restoring TAZARA to its former standards, and commended Chinese President Xi Jinping, Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan and Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema for their crucial roles in supporting this milestone.

a2915.speaker: Frank Tayali, Zambia’s Minister for Transport and Logistics
a2915.name: Frank Tayali
a2915.title: Zambia’s Minister for Transport and Logistics
a2915.speech: Underscored that the agreement had been signed at a timely moment, and said that once the upgrades are complete the railway is expected to operate more efficiently and expand its capacity to transport both passengers and cargo for the countries that depend on its services.

a2915.speaker: Dai Hegen, Chairman of China Railway Construction Corporation Limited (CRCC)
a2915.name: Dai Hegen
a2915.title: Chairman of China Railway Construction Corporation Limited (CRCC)
a2915.speech: Outlined other successful projects the company has undertaken across the African continent, reinforcing China’s commitment to infrastructure development in the region.

a3035.speaker: Jeror Cole Banggalu, Minister of Youth and Sports of Liberia
a3035.name: Jeror Cole Banggalu
a3035.title: Minister of Youth and Sports of Liberia
a3035.speech: Announced an allocation of US$1 million to reintroduce the National Youth Service Program and emphasized government's commitment to the Cadet Program, stating, “We are serious about this initiative and will ensure its successful implementation alongside UNDP Liberia.” ; “The government is dedicated to the welfare of young people; therefore, it is our responsibility to improve the lives of our citizens, especially our youth.”

a3035.speaker: Press release (Ministry of Youth and Sports)
a3035.name: Press release (Ministry of Youth and Sports)
a3035.speech: According to a press release, he highlighted the success of past cadets, many of whom have secured permanent roles in government following their internships, spoke of efforts to expand the program and expressed gratitude to UNDP for the partnership.

a3035.speaker: Louis Kuukpen, Deputy Resident Representative for Programme, UNDP Liberia
a3035.name: Louis Kuukpen
a3035.title: Deputy Resident Representative for Programme, UNDP Liberia
a3035.speech: Lauded the government's ongoing efforts in youth development, asserting that investing in youth is an investment in Liberia's future: “At UNDP, we strongly believe that investing in youth is investing in the future. Young people are not only the leaders of tomorrow, they are the changemakers of today. Yet across Africa, and here in Liberia, youth unemployment remains a pressing challenge. Programs like the NCP are essential to breaking that cycle by equipping young people with practical skills, professional exposure, and confidence to pursue dignified livelihoods.” ; said the cadet program is not a temporary placement but a launchpad for careers, innovation, and entrepreneurship, and urged cadets who will be recruited this year to take full advantage of the opportunity to learn, grow, contribute, and dream boldly.

a3035.speaker: Kolubah Yekeh, speaking on behalf of the Commerce Minister of Liberia
a3035.name: Kolubah Yekeh
a3035.title: speaking on behalf of the Commerce Minister of Liberia
a3035.speech: Emphasized the importance of the program, calling for increased support from other partners for the next 5 years.

a3240.speaker: Bana Ibrahim, whistleblower and member of the Patriotic Front for Sovereignty (civil society organisation)
a3240.name: Bana Ibrahim
a3240.title: whistleblower and member of the Patriotic Front for Sovereignty (civil society organisation)
a3240.speech: Stressed that the first added value brought by SONIDEP's exploitation of these blocks in terms of the struggle for sovereignty in the petroleum sector is that "this is the very first time that from start to finish the oil exploitation process will be carried out by a national company" ; specified in an interview granted to the ANP that there will be no intervention by any outside economic patron in the exploration or the exploitation, "which means that the only interests that will be put forward are Nigerien interests, since both SONIDEP and the State that grants are one and the same" ; finally expressed his satisfaction that the Nigerien people can have access to petroleum products under conditions capable of ensuring social equity and the sustainable development of the country.

a3594.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.name: Temitope Ilori
a3594.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.speech: revealed that 1.6 million of the estimated two million Nigerians living with HIV are currently undergoing treatment; explained that the 2024 World AIDS Day theme aims to raise awareness about HIV, honour lives impacted by the epidemic, and prioritise eliminating AIDS among children: "Nigeria has an HIV prevalence rate of 1.4% among the general population, with approximately 160,000 children aged 0-14 living with the virus."

a3594.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.name: Temitope Ilori
a3594.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.speech: noted significant challenges in preventing mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), with current coverage below 33%: "We have engaged stakeholders to co-create a sustainability road map, ensuring that gains in the HIV response are preserved and government structures remain functional."

a3594.speaker: Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.name: Temitope Ilori
a3594.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a3594.speech: called for collective efforts to break stigma and improve equity: "On this World AIDS Day, I urge all Nigerians to join hands with NACA to break stigma, embrace equity, and drive action to eliminate HIV among children. We must empower vulnerable groups, especially women, to access life-saving services and live with dignity. Together, we can achieve an AIDS-free Nigeria by 2030."

a3594.speaker: Leo Zekeng, Country Director of UNAIDS
a3594.name: Leo Zekeng
a3594.title: Country Director of UNAIDS
a3594.speech: stressed the importance of sustainability and political commitment to achieve the 2030 goal: "Ending AIDS requires increased domestic resources and collaboration among government agencies, private sectors, and health organisations to allocate more funds for the response."

a3594.speaker: Patrick Dakum, CEO of the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN), represented by Olayemi Olupitan
a3594.name: Patrick Dakum
a3594.title: CEO of the Institute of Human Virology Nigeria (IHVN), represented by Olayemi Olupitan
a3594.speech: emphasised a holistic approach to combating HIV and tuberculosis (TB): "World AIDS Day reminds us of our collective responsibility to ensure no one is left behind in the fight against HIV/AIDS."

a3594.speaker: Funmi Adesanya, Nigeria Country Coordinator for the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), represented by Emerson Evans
a3594.name: Funmi Adesanya
a3594.title: Nigeria Country Coordinator for the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR), represented by Emerson Evans
a3594.speech: highlighted the need to expand prevention efforts and invest in healthcare systems, and called for scaling up evidence-based strategies like Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) and harm reduction services, especially for marginalised groups: "Investing in research, developing innovative vaccines, and creating long-acting treatment regimens is critical to improving outcomes and reducing transmission."

a3665.speaker: IMF research chapter (cited)
a3665.name: IMF research chapter (cited)
a3665.speech: "In secular jurisdictions such as the United Kingdom and the United States, the courts have demonstrated willingness and capability to enforce Islamic finance contracts, despite the secular nature of these jurisdictions."

a3678.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a3678.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a3678.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a3678.speech: Speaking to the press after the swearing-in of the new Government, stressed that there is “no indication from the American administration that the MCC, the package that is intended for Cabo Verde, will be affected”; clarified that the 90-day suspension of aid will have no immediate impact, since the projects of the third compact are still in the drafting phase and should only be implemented in 2026 ; “90 days on the horizon of 2026 does not affect [it],” he stressed.

a3678.speaker: Ulisses Correia e Silva, Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a3678.name: Ulisses Correia e Silva
a3678.title: Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a3678.speech: On deportations: hopes that Cabo Verdeans will not be affected on a massive scale — “The Cabo Verdean community is well integrated in the United States”; reaffirmed that Cabo Verde has a national programme to guarantee the reintegration of deportees, assuring that they “will be well integrated and well received” in Cabo Verde ; “Wherever a Cabo Verdean may be, if he returns, he will always be well received,” he concluded.

a3678.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3678.name: Kyeh Kim
a3678.title: Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a3678.speech: Said last October that the third MCC compact, which aims to promote strategic investments in sectors such as land, air, maritime, digital and human connectivity and mobility, is due to be signed in April 2026.

a3690.speaker: Sagnarigu Municipal Directorate of Education
a3690.name: Sagnarigu Municipal Directorate of Education
a3690.speech: Has appealed for support to address the myriad of challenges facing education in the municipality ; indicated that one of the major challenges confronting education is the lack of office space, which has been hindering its operation.

a3690.speaker: Andani Zakaria Abdulai, Municipal Education Training Officer, Sagnarigu
a3690.name: Andani Zakaria Abdulai
a3690.title: Municipal Education Training Officer, Sagnarigu
a3690.speech: Speaking at the 2023/2024 education review, indicated that the directorate was currently operating from abandoned offices at the Tamale Senior High School, a situation that had persisted since the municipality’s inception in 2012 ; “The lack of office space has made it difficult for us to work effectively. We are forced to share a few offices, which impacts our operations. If the school ever needs the building back, we would have nowhere to go,” he lamented.

a3690.speaker: Andani Zakaria Abdulai, Municipal Education Training Officer, Sagnarigu
a3690.name: Andani Zakaria Abdulai
a3690.title: Municipal Education Training Officer, Sagnarigu
a3690.speech: Added that the municipality was facing a furniture deficit of about 17,000 and that the situation had forced most school children to study on the bare floor ; “most of the schools’ structures are dilapidated, with poor ventilation, which is seriously affecting teaching and learning” ; said though the municipal assembly was doing its best to rescue the situation, more support was needed to help address the challenge.

a3690.speaker: Ayuba Abukari, Head of Programmes at School for Life
a3690.name: Ayuba Abukari
a3690.title: Head of Programmes at School for Life
a3690.speech: Reiterated his outfit’s commitment towards continuous collaboration with the assembly and the GES to improve learning outcomes.

a3690.speaker: Mahmud Osman, Coordinating Director of the Sagnarigu Municipal Assembly
a3690.name: Mahmud Osman
a3690.title: Coordinating Director of the Sagnarigu Municipal Assembly
a3690.speech: Acknowledged the challenges facing education in the municipality and assured that the assembly would incorporate some of the challenges in its 2025 development plan.

a3695.speaker: Nana Kwame Bediako, presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.name: Nana Kwame Bediako
a3695.title: presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.speech: Shared his plans to improve the lives of Ghanaians if elected in the 2024 general elections, outlining three main areas of focus: job creation, efficient use of natural resources, and strengthening Ghana’s economic independence ; emphasized the need for every region in Ghana to benefit from its resources, stating that regions should create jobs and wealth locally to reduce dependence on opportunities in cities like Accra: “Every Ghanaian should have access to opportunities where they live,” he said, comparing Ghana’s potential to cities in countries like England where wealth is more evenly distributed.

a3695.speaker: Nana Kwame Bediako, presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.name: Nana Kwame Bediako
a3695.title: presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.speech: Criticised the current underuse of water resources, highlighting their potential for logistics and agriculture; proposed developing irrigation systems to ensure year-round farming and creating water transport systems, such as ferries, to connect regions and facilitate trade; shared an example from Afram Plains, where farmers face delays in transporting yams due to limited ferry services, and suggested investing in yam processing factories to produce and export powdered yam to markets like Nigeria: “This will create jobs and boost our economy,” he said.

a3695.speaker: Nana Kwame Bediako, presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.name: Nana Kwame Bediako
a3695.title: presidential candidate for the New Force party
a3695.speech: Said the third part of his plan is to expand Ghana’s power supply and make energy affordable, explaining this will attract investors and support industries; called for better management of Ghana’s natural resources, such as gold, which he said are currently exploited by foreign companies without transferring skills to locals; proposed stricter regulations to ensure foreign companies operate in ways that benefit Ghana: “We can welcome investors, but they must help build our nation, not just take our wealth,” he said ; acknowledged the challenges Ghana faces, including economic and social crises, and urged the youth to join his movement for change: “I represent a force of hope, a force that can lead Ghana toward a brighter future,” Bediako concluded.

a3805.speaker: Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a3805.name: Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC)
a3805.speech: has said Africa faces an “unprecedented surge” in public health emergencies, adding pressure on the continent’s already fragile health systems ; said the surge in disease outbreaks has placed “immense pressure on already fragile health systems, exposing deep-seated vulnerabilities and severely weakening the continent’s capacity for timely and effective response.”

a3805.speaker: Africa CDC
a3805.name: Africa CDC
a3805.speech: has called on African countries to strengthen innovative domestic financing mechanisms to address the emerging and existing public health challenges across the continent ; noting that Africa’s health sector is facing a financing crisis, driven by a sharp decline of 70 percent in official development assistance from 2021 to 2025 and deep-rooted structural vulnerabilities, underscored the urgent need to address health financing challenges in the continent through domestic resource mobilisation and innovative financing mechanisms.

a3805.speaker: Africa CDC
a3805.name: Africa CDC
a3805.speech: said the “sudden and significant reduction” in official development assistance has critically impacted health outcomes across Africa, directly causing disruptions in essential health services, including downgrading efforts on the response to ongoing outbreaks such as mpox, ebola, Marburg, and measles.

a3805.speaker: Africa CDC Annual Report-2024 and Africa’s Health Financing in a New Era report (data from the African Union’s specialised healthcare agency)
a3805.name: Africa CDC Annual Report-2024 and Africa’s Health Financing in a New Era report (data from the African Union’s specialised healthcare agency)
a3805.speech: showed that the African continent, over the past 24 months, has witnessed an “unprecedented surge in public health emergencies,” rising by 41 percent — from 152 disease outbreaks in 2022 to 213 in 2024.

a3864.speaker: Dr Ekwow Spio-Garbrah, Board Chairman of Onesta Ghana Ltd and former Minister of Trade and Industry
a3864.name: Dr Ekwow Spio-Garbrah
a3864.title: Board Chairman of Onesta Ghana Ltd and former Minister of Trade and Industry
a3864.speech: said the ROPP aims to make palm oil a strategic crop, akin to cocoa, in Ghana's agribusiness agenda ; “I am very glad this vision is here. For the first 10,000 hectares alone, we estimate a need for $50 million in investment.” ; noted that Ghana, like Malaysia, has the potential to use oil palm to drive national development and economic transformation.

a3864.speaker: John Setor Dumelo, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and MP for Ayawaso West
a3864.name: John Setor Dumelo
a3864.title: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and MP for Ayawaso West
a3864.speech: pledged full government support for the project ; “Investment in the palm oil sector has the potential to provide jobs, improve local economies, and reduce rural poverty.” ; “We at the Ministry of Agric will give Onesta Ghana the conducive environment and support needed to accomplish this resounding vision.” ; disclosed that the Ministry of Finance is in the process of establishing a Real Sector Division to identify and invest in high-impact sectors, including agribusiness and responsible mining.

a3864.speaker: Maxwell Commey, Executive Director of Onesta Ghana Ltd and CEO of Oro Oil Ghana Ltd
a3864.name: Maxwell Commey
a3864.title: Executive Director of Onesta Ghana Ltd and CEO of Oro Oil Ghana Ltd
a3864.speech: highlighted the integrated nature of the ROPP ; “ROPP will offer end-to-end solutions—from cultivation to processing and refining—delivering quality products while promoting economic growth and environmental sustainability.” ; “This PPP will enhance food security, create employment, and deliver value to stakeholders while upholding environmental and social safety.”

a3955.speaker: Zimplats (trading update)
a3955.name: Zimplats (trading update)
a3955.speech: In a trading update for the period, Zimplats said a total of US$4,5 million was transferred from operating costs as milled throughput…

a4023.speaker: Sosthène Boko, works director
a4023.name: Sosthène Boko
a4023.title: works director
a4023.speech: Reported on the completed works: for the first component, as part of the construction of the bridge, the supports, the pre-slabs and the 12 planned beams have been completed; currently under way is the threading of cables to go into the composition of the pre-stressed concrete ; projected for the beginning of next October the repair of certain dikes which the waters have cracked in places, with the rest of the works — from the pouring of the beams onto the supports to the laying of the 24 cm-wide compression slab — spread over October and November ; clarified that the embankment of the 300 m Zounhouè-Athiémé road is continuing at the same time as the manufacture of the paving stones expected for its surfacing.

a4023.speaker: Boni Yayi, President of the Republic of Benin
a4023.name: Boni Yayi
a4023.title: President of the Republic of Benin
a4023.speech: Remained firm about respecting the contractual deadline and, keen to see the works finished next November, immediately promised to intervene against the flood risk at Nangbéto with the officials of the body concerned ; “Athiémé is a rich commune, but the people are poor today. With this structure, Athiémé will always be a rich commune and the people will be rich. Mr Mayor, everything will change, I have come to hand you the key” — saying he was satisfied with the explanations provided, and predicting the revival of the commune’s economy around the road infrastructure and the influx of foreign communities.

a4023.speaker: Joseph Anani Amavi, mayor of Athiémé
a4023.name: Joseph Anani Amavi
a4023.title: mayor of Athiémé
a4023.speech: Reported the interest the Lebanese community already has in his commune: “Together with the communal council we have taken a decree declaring the zone of public utility” ; pleaded for his commune to be taken into account in the investment of the funds granted by the second compact of the Millennium Challenge Account (MCA).

a4029.speaker: US Embassy in Juba
a4029.name: US Embassy in Juba
a4029.speech: Has called on stakeholders in the humanitarian and development assistance sector to commit to a zero-tolerance policy on sexual exploitation, abuse, and harassment ; emphasized the importance of upholding the dignity and safety of all individuals by actively preventing such acts ; in a statement to Eye Radio newsroom on Friday, the Embassy said: “This Day is important for accountability and protection against violations about USAID programming, critical to the access of humanitarian and development work.”

a4029.speaker: US Embassy in Juba
a4029.name: US Embassy in Juba
a4029.speech: Called for prompt investigations into all allegations, with support from the transitional government authorities ; stressed the need for swift and appropriate actions to be taken against the perpetrators while ensuring that survivors receive the necessary support ; went on to urge all those who participate in the humanitarian and development aid sector to promote a culture of accountability and encourage the reporting of concerns without fear of retaliation.

a4075.speaker: Eugene Arhin, Director of Communications at the Presidency (statement, Office of the President)
a4075.name: Eugene Arhin
a4075.title: Director of Communications at the Presidency (statement, Office of the President)
a4075.speech: Clarified that Nana Bediatuo Asante is in stable condition at a hospital in the United States following an illness. "The Office of the President wishes to inform the public about the health status of Nana Bediatuo Asante, Secretary to the President. Following the conclusion of the meeting of the 79th United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York, in the United States of America, where he served as a key member of President Akufo-Addo's delegation, Nana Bediatuo Asante stayed behind to conduct further government business. He then began to feel unwell, and was subsequently admitted to hospital. He is currently in stable condition and responding well to treatment." ; "We ask for continued prayers and support for him and his family during this difficult period. Further updates will be provided when necessary."

a4075.speaker: The medical team treating Nana Bediatuo Asante
a4075.name: The medical team treating Nana Bediatuo Asante
a4075.speech: According to the medical team, Nana Bediatuo Asante's recovery is on track, and "we remain hopeful for his swift return to full strength."

a4108.speaker: UNRWA and Israeli allies such as Germany
a4108.name: UNRWA and Israeli allies such as Germany
a4108.speech: say the ban will cause the total collapse of aid operations in Gaza.

a4108.speaker: Israel
a4108.name: Israel
a4108.speech: claims that a dozen UNRWA employees were involved in the deadly assault.

a4108.speaker: Jonas Gahr Store, Norwegian Prime Minister
a4108.name: Jonas Gahr Store
a4108.title: Norwegian Prime Minister
a4108.speech: said in a statement that Norway was "requesting that the ICJ pronounces on Israel's obligations to facilitate humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian population, delivered by international organisations, including the UN and states" ; He said Norway would submit a resolution to the UN General Assembly with the request that the ICJ give an advisory opinion on the matter.

a4108.speaker: Espen Barth Eide, Norwegian Foreign Minister
a4108.name: Espen Barth Eide
a4108.title: Norwegian Foreign Minister
a4108.speech: "The Israeli government's policy is making it increasingly difficult for Palestinians to access life-saving assistance and basic services such as healthcare and education" ; said the UNRWA ban would have "severe consequences for millions of civilians already living in the most dire of circumstances," adding that it "also undermines the stability of the entire Middle East" ; "Israel's behaviour contravenes international law and undermines efforts to establish a viable Palestinian state and the two-state solution."

a4169.speaker: John Steenhuisen, Democratic Alliance (DA) leader and South African agriculture minister
a4169.name: John Steenhuisen
a4169.title: Democratic Alliance (DA) leader and South African agriculture minister
a4169.speech: Said the 30% tariff Donald Trump imposed on South Africa's exports to the U.S. will stay unless the government changes some domestic race policies such as affirmative action ; “It is very clear that while we’ve been negotiating on a trade track, the issues with the Trump administration are deeper than that” ; “These cover things (like)… expropriation without compensation. It deals with some of the labour laws in the country and also the racial legislation.”

a4169.speaker: John Steenhuisen, Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.name: John Steenhuisen
a4169.title: Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.speech: Added that South Africa’s membership of the BRICS bloc centred around Brazil, Russia, India and China – and which aims to challenge U.S. hegemony – was also an issue for the Trump administration.

a4169.speaker: John Steenhuisen, Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.name: John Steenhuisen
a4169.title: Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.speech: Said he thought it was “odd” that the Trump administration was linking such issues to trade ; “Just as we would not seek to interfere in the domestic politics of the United States of America, we would expect that issues that relate to our own sovereignty are also respected.”

a4169.speaker: John Steenhuisen, Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.name: John Steenhuisen
a4169.title: Democratic Alliance (DA) leader
a4169.speech: Said these laws could not be changed overnight to please the U.S. because they have to be debated at length in parliament ; said he thought it might improve relations if South Africa sent a “signal” that it intended to move in that direction ; “My worry is that we’re going to continue to negotiate on tariffs and trade… (and) the 30% is going to remain.”

a4169.speaker: Democratic Alliance (DA) party
a4169.name: Democratic Alliance (DA) party
a4169.speech: Says South Africa's Broad-based Black Economic Empowerment (BEE) Act and other laws should be replaced with non-racial measures to boost the economy and create jobs, such as removing red tape and simplifying business licensing.

a4169.speaker: African National Congress (ANC)
a4169.name: African National Congress (ANC)
a4169.speech: Regards BEE as a flagship policy meant to address apartheid’s legacy ; says concerns over the Expropriation Act signed this year, which enables the government to address inequalities in land ownership in rare cases by seizing it for redistribution, are overblown.

a4339.speaker: Kelvin Remen, deputy chief of party for the Feed the Future Tanzania, Tuhifadhi Chakula project
a4339.name: Kelvin Remen
a4339.title: deputy chief of party for the Feed the Future Tanzania, Tuhifadhi Chakula project
a4339.speech: Highlighted the necessity of the demonstration sessions and mentioned significant issues such as limited access to finance and lack of awareness of post-harvest management technologies such as harvest technologies, storage techniques, processing methods technologies and packaging solutions ; "This initiative aims to transform horticultural practices in Zanzibar, paving the way for sustainable growth and resilience within the industry", adding: "Our forward-thinking approach promises to uplift the livelihoods of farmers, ensuring a brighter future."

a4339.speaker: Engineer Indris Abdullah, Officer in charge, Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, Natural Resources and Livestock (Zanzibar)
a4339.name: Engineer Indris Abdullah
a4339.title: Officer in charge, Ministry of Agriculture, Irrigation, Natural Resources and Livestock (Zanzibar)
a4339.speech: Underscored the importance of sharing knowledge and experiences among farmers: "The event not only focused on improving postharvest management practices but also facilitated building a robust network of horticulture farmers in Pemba." ; commended TAHA for its role in providing professional agricultural guidance, advancing food security and helping to link farmers with markets and financial institutions, and lauded their advocacy efforts to create a favourable business environment for the horticultural industry in Zanzibar.

a4349.speaker: Sheila Siwela, Zambia's Ambassador to the United States of America
a4349.name: Sheila Siwela
a4349.title: Zambia's Ambassador to the United States of America
a4349.speech: "The choice for Zambia to host the AGOA Forum has come at the right time considering that the country's economic performance and governance record have been on the positive in the past three years" ; observes that financial institutions such as the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) and the Corporate Council on Africa (CCA) are agreed that Zambia is on the right footing ; notes that top US international credit rating agencies Fitch and Standard and Poor have, in the recent one month, independently given Zambia a "B plus" rating, a sign that Zambia is a good destination for foreign direct investment and that the country could be eligible to access funding from international bond markets ; adds that Zambia should not miss this opportunity of showcasing her potential as the next best destination in investment at this Forum considering that the country is enjoying increased construction and rising copper prices, a rebound in tourism, improved agricultural performance and most of all the peace and political stability that the country has enjoyed since independence ; "The bottom line is that Zambia is now ready for business. The AGOA Forum will be a great opportunity for business people from Africa and the USA to interact for the sole purpose of creating partnerships and opening up new businesses in both continents."

a4349.speaker: Felix Mutati, Minister of Commerce, Trade and Industry (speech read for him by Davis Sampa, Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Vice President)
a4349.name: Felix Mutati
a4349.title: Minister of Commerce, Trade and Industry (speech read for him by Davis Sampa, Permanent Secretary in the Office of the Vice President)
a4349.speech: Was recently quoted in the media as saying that Zambia's export figures to the USA including the General System of Preferences (GSP) provisions of the AGOA Act had risen steadily to US$10.9 million in 2008 from US$361,000 in 2006 ; however said the decline in exports posted in 2009 of US$33.7 billion is consistent with a decline from US$66.2 billion worth of exports from all AGOA eligible sub-Saharan African countries in 2008 due to the global financial crisis ; said currently, 90 percent of all AGOA exports to the USA are energy related exports, with other notable products being textiles and garments, automobiles, processed agricultural products, leather products, machine parts, metals, gemstones and handicrafts.

a4349.speaker: Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), Washington DC
a4349.name: Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR)
a4349.title: Washington DC
a4349.speech: According to the USTR, for the period 2009 Zambia's main exports to the US included base metal (cobalt), precious stones (emeralds), spices, coffee, tea and metal ores ; the USTR states that Zambia was the 167th largest goods trading partner of the USA with $67 million in total (two way) goods trade during 2009 ; according to the USTR website, the USA exported $59 million worth of goods to Zambia and in return Zambia exported a total of $9 million of goods to the USA, making the US goods trade surplus with Zambia $50 million in 2009.

a4349.speaker: US Department of Commerce (official statistics)
a4349.name: US Department of Commerce (official statistics)
a4349.speech: According to official statistics from the US Department of Commerce, the collective exports of Angola, Nigeria and South Africa for the year 2010 were valued at over US$3 billion.

a4349.speaker: Zambia Association of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ZACCI)
a4349.name: Zambia Association of Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ZACCI)
a4349.speech: Supports the hosting of the 2011 AGOA Forum conference as it will help Zambian entrepreneurs to understand how to penetrate the US market.

a4349.speaker: Geoffrey Sakulanda, ZACCI President
a4349.name: Geoffrey Sakulanda
a4349.title: ZACCI President
a4349.speech: Says the benefits from AGOA would be clear for all to see because Zambian entrepreneurs would have an opportunity to discuss partnership arrangements with their US counterparts which would enable them to export high quality products into the American market ; was also of the belief that the AGOA Forum in Lusaka would give local Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) an opportunity to exhibit their products and at the same time make business linkages with international SMEs.

a4450.speaker: Survey/research on US public opinion (cited)
a4450.name: Survey/research on US public opinion (cited)
a4450.speech: Research reveals that more than 60% of Americans state that funding for humanitarian aid is "wasted on corruption or administrative fees."

a4450.speaker: Study on Portuguese public opinion (cited)
a4450.name: Study on Portuguese public opinion (cited)
a4450.speech: A study shows that although the Portuguese consider helping the poorest countries to be important, the majority of them want something in return.

a4450.speaker: Minister of Education of Cabo Verde
a4450.name: Minister of Education of Cabo Verde
a4450.speech: In an interview with the Lusa news agency, argued that it is "necessary to create the foundations for the full officialisation of the Cape Verdean language", but also stressed that the training of the first Cape Verdean-language teachers will never take "less than 10 years."

a4450.speaker: Amanda Robertson, Portuguese-language spokesperson for the US Department of State
a4450.name: Amanda Robertson
a4450.title: Portuguese-language spokesperson for the US Department of State
a4450.speech: In conversation with Expresso das Ilhas, highlighted that although "America First" has guided US policy under the Trump administrations, that does not mean the country will work in isolation from the rest of the world: relations with other nations will continue to be fostered, and the expectation is that they too will gain from the approach and become more prosperous and secure. Topics addressed ranged from immigration to the suspension of USAID, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and South Africa.

a4487.speaker: Sarah B.M. Bamie, Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
a4487.name: Sarah B.M. Bamie
a4487.title: Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
a4487.speech: Underscored the need for a comprehensive legal framework to address the unique challenges faced by rural women in the fisheries and aquaculture sectors, including ensuring that women had equal access to resources such as land, credit and training: "By establishing laws that protect women's rights and promote gender equality, we can foster an environment where women can thrive as entrepreneurs and leaders within the fisheries value chain."

a4487.speaker: Sarah B.M. Bamie, Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
a4487.name: Sarah B.M. Bamie
a4487.title: Upper East Regional Director of the Fisheries Commission
a4487.speech: Called for the implementation of gender-responsive policies through which the needs and perspectives of women would be integrated into all fisheries management and development programmes, indicating that such a move would enhance women's participation in decision-making processes, thereby ensuring that their voices and contributions were heard and valued.

a4487.speaker: Zinabu Abdulai, Director, Resilience and Social Inclusion, USAID-funded Market Systems and Resilience (MSR) Activity
a4487.name: Zinabu Abdulai
a4487.title: Director, Resilience and Social Inclusion, USAID-funded Market Systems and Resilience (MSR) Activity
a4487.speech: Said under the MSR activity, a series of entrepreneurship initiatives have been rolled out to empower women to run their businesses effectively: "We are assisting women to do their respective trades better by adopting best practices to produce commodities and products on a large scale to meet the growing demands of the larger market."

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative and disability rights advocate
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative and disability rights advocate
a4811.speech: “I believe disability does not mean inability because everyone regardless of their physical condition deserves the opportunity to live their dreams,” ; “I faced many barriers in terms of resources and support. Most schools I attended had no special needs teachers. I often struggled to keep up.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
