a4811.speech: disclosed that the name Tikuyana is Tumbuka, which means ‘We are all Equal’ ; “The initiative came out of the desire to address the barriers and inequalities that people with disabilities face, particularly those with hearing impairment” ; “Our initiative aims to promote inclusivity and equal opportunities for people with disabilities. We recognise that disability is not a limitation, but a natural part of human diversity. We strive to create a society where everyone can participate. Our main focus area is on education, advocacy and economic empowerment.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: said quality education is the future for success, and observed that economic empowerment is a key aspect of the initiative as vocational training and economic opportunities can help individuals with disabilities gain financial independence ; “Many young people with disabilities drop out of school early because of the lack of support and understanding. We want to change that narrative by creating environments where they feel seen, heard and empowered.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: noted challenges people with disabilities face in accessing education and employment: “Inaccessible curriculum that doesn’t fit the needs of those with disabilities, inadequate support services such as braille materials/ sign language interpreter and limited availability of assistive technologies. When it comes to employment, people with disabilities face discrimination as some may be deemed unfit,” and said these challenges can lead to limited job opportunities and lower career advancements.

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: said that through Tikuyana, vocational training programmes have improved and young people own businesses ; “We have made young people with disabilities become role models by inspiring others to achieve their goals and dreams regardless of their abilities” ; “Our work has shown that through the right support and better opportunities, everyone can still make contributions to the community.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: recounted: “There were no special needs teachers and the curriculum wasn’t inclusive. Visiting a school for learners with hearing impairments and discovering alarming issues, low secondary school enrollment, lack of role models, inadequate resources and stigma. That was my turning point and I knew I had to be part of the change. After completing my bachelor’s degree, I officially began her advocacy journey.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: said of her international engagements (including a Green Economy Summit in the United States sponsored by USaid Malawi): “Through these experiences, I gained knowledge on youth-led solutions and innovative approaches to advocacy. They helped me to become a more effective leader and gave me the courage to share my story with the world.”

a4811.speaker: Malumbo Mkinga, founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.name: Malumbo Mkinga
a4811.title: founder of the Tikuyana initiative
a4811.speech: “We envision a world where people with disabilities are leaders, decision makers and innovators, where no child is left behind because of their hearing, vision, or mobility. My dream is simple, to see an inclusive world where everyone has the opportunity to rise.”

a4857.speaker: Abdul Farah, 73, resident of Gode Wereda, Shabelle Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.name: Abdul Farah
a4857.title: 73, resident of Gode Wereda, Shabelle Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.speech: "Not even to eat," said of his surviving animals, which are not healthy enough to sell ; "We live on the edge" ; "The carcasses of dead animals are piled up in the streets," Abdul told Fortune.

a4857.speaker: Abdul Farah, 73, resident of Gode Wereda, Shabelle Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.name: Abdul Farah
a4857.title: 73, resident of Gode Wereda, Shabelle Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.speech: "If the drought continues like this, livestock populations will plummet to almost zero," Abdul fears.

a4857.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UN-OCHA) (tweet)
a4857.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UN-OCHA) (tweet)
a4857.speech: "For the first time in 4 decades, Ethiopia is experiencing a prolonged drought with three poor rainy seasons in a row," reads a tweet.

a4857.speaker: Eyasu Mekonnen, doctoral student in climate-smart agriculture and biodiversity conservation, Haramaya University
a4857.name: Eyasu Mekonnen
a4857.title: doctoral student in climate-smart agriculture and biodiversity conservation, Haramaya University
a4857.speech: Says the drought cycles are becoming more frequent in the Horn of Africa due to temperature changes in the Indian Ocean ; "Drought is a vicious cycle, and people are going from one crisis to another with very little breathing room to take stock."

a4857.speaker: Eyasu Mekonnen, doctoral student in climate-smart agriculture and biodiversity conservation, Haramaya University
a4857.name: Eyasu Mekonnen
a4857.title: doctoral student in climate-smart agriculture and biodiversity conservation, Haramaya University
a4857.speech: Argues that a better understanding of what the future may hold will help people living in arid areas cope with the consequences of climate change: "Enhancing irrigation schemes and diversifying rural livelihoods through social protection and introducing cash-transfer programmes can be useful tools" ; "Governments of poor countries should recognise the traditional approach of mitigating drought is no longer viable" ; urges officials consider resettlement programmes in response: "The relocation of herds and the use of special reserved areas can be useful strategies."

a4857.speaker: Abdulfatah Mohammed, deputy head of the Somali Regional State's bureau for disaster prevention and preparedness
a4857.name: Abdulfatah Mohammed
a4857.title: deputy head of the Somali Regional State's bureau for disaster prevention and preparedness
a4857.speech: Disclosed that herders report losses of more than 70pc of their animals, and that the death toll has surpassed 1.4 million heads of livestock in the Somali Regional State.

a4857.speaker: Adem Ahmed, administrator of Shabelle Zone
a4857.name: Adem Ahmed
a4857.title: administrator of Shabelle Zone
a4857.speech: Says 17 trucks have been assigned to distribute water to the residents of his jurisdiction ; "It's impossible to assist all affected people."

a4857.speaker: Abiy Ahmed (PhD), Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4857.name: Abiy Ahmed (PhD)
a4857.title: Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a4857.speech: "We'll scale up the provision of water trucks, food, animal feed and essential medicines," he said during his visit to Jigjiga. "We will accelerate the small dam projects we've embarked upon to support water management in lowland areas as a pathway to circumventing future droughts."

a4857.speaker: Ibrahim Alefe, resident of Shekosh Wereda, Korahe Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.name: Ibrahim Alefe
a4857.title: resident of Shekosh Wereda, Korahe Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.speech: Says the worst loss has been that of his camels, of a herd of 65 nearly all of which have died over the past year: "It's unheard of, I have never known them to die like this."

a4857.speaker: Ibrahim Alefe, resident of Shekosh Wereda, Korahe Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.name: Ibrahim Alefe
a4857.title: resident of Shekosh Wereda, Korahe Zone, Somali Regional State
a4857.speech: "We're only receiving enough to sustain our lives here," he said of the temporary shelter housing his displaced family. "I'm hoping for a miracle at this stage."

a4857.speaker: Abdulnasir Hassen, early warning and response coordinator for Korahe Zone
a4857.name: Abdulnasir Hassen
a4857.title: early warning and response coordinator for Korahe Zone
a4857.speech: Said that of the 10 weredas of Korahe where close to 400,000 people need emergency relief assistance, only three are receiving aid: "The assistance we're receiving is insufficient. We're prioritising the most affected areas."

a4857.speaker: Mechi Korecha, 26, resident of Arero Wereda, Borena Zone, Oromia Regional State
a4857.name: Mechi Korecha
a4857.title: 26, resident of Arero Wereda, Borena Zone, Oromia Regional State
a4857.speech: "All I can think about is my child's future," he told Fortune, saying his chief concern is the safety and health of his already malnourished child.

a4857.speaker: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) report
a4857.name: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) report
a4857.speech: Reports that malnutrition cases are doubling in Oromia Regional State and that incidents of diarrheal cases among children under the age of five are increasing.

a4857.speaker: Persons close to the matter (anonymous)
a4857.name: Persons close to the matter (anonymous)
a4857.speech: Said the federal government has appealed to the World Food Programme to provide an additional million quintals of rice and nutritious food to the Somali Regional State.

a4857.speaker: UN report published last month
a4857.name: UN report published last month
a4857.speech: Estimated 22 million Ethiopians would require emergency humanitarian assistance worth 1.4 billion dollars this year, with close to 900 million dollars in funding yet to be raised; urgent action is needed to reverse deepening drought impacts in southern and eastern Ethiopia, reads the report, whose authors described the situation as a "continuous drought-like condition" and viewed what is unfolding in southern Oromia and Somali regions with "particular concern."

a4966.speaker: United Nations
a4966.name: United Nations
a4966.speech: Said more than 45,000 people have been affected by flash floods in Somalia since mid-April, with at least four people killed in the rapidly rising waters.

a4966.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4966.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4966.speech: Warned the flooding came at a time when NGOs, often the frontline responders, are "facing crippling funding reductions that have severely limited their ability to respond to emerging needs" ; noted that "Currently, many humanitarian organisations in areas where the flash flooding is occurring have been forced to pause, scale back, or even close their critical programmes."

a4966.speaker: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4966.name: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a4966.speech: Detailed that roughly 6,000 people were displaced in the Middle Shabelle region after the Shabelle River burst its banks on 29 April; said families have sought refuge in makeshift camps on higher ground but are "facing acute shortages of food, clean water, and healthcare" ; "The flooding swept away homes and inundated crops, disrupting livelihoods in one of Somalia's most agriculturally vital regions" ; said that the day before, some 9,500 people were also displaced in central Galmudug State after light to moderate rains caused flash floods.

a5027.speaker: Hawa Sharif Ali, 49, internally displaced mother living in the Al-Adalada camp, Mogadishu
a5027.name: Hawa Sharif Ali
a5027.title: 49, internally displaced mother living in the Al-Adalada camp, Mogadishu
a5027.speech: “I give priority to my children’s health. Every time I give birth, I bring my baby here” ; “We cannot afford to go to private hospitals, but this centre is accessible for us. Today, my son received his measles vaccine to complete his immunisations. All my other children have also completed their vaccinations, and I am satisfied.”

a5027.speaker: Mukhtar Derow Luqmaan, supervisor of the Sinkadheer health centre
a5027.name: Mukhtar Derow Luqmaan
a5027.title: supervisor of the Sinkadheer health centre
a5027.speech: “Most of the people we serve here are mothers and children from the nearby camps. For them, this centre is vital.”

a5027.speaker: Dr Renée Van de Weerdt, WHO Representative in Somalia
a5027.name: Dr Renée Van de Weerdt
a5027.title: WHO Representative in Somalia
a5027.speech: “Thanks to the unwavering support of donors such as ECHO, WHO has been able to bring life-saving health care to drought-affected communities, offering families a chance to recover. Today, we are strengthening the resilience of the health system to meet their current needs and to cope better with any crises to come.”

a5155.speaker: Wondafrash Assefa, Public Relation Head of the Ministry of Public Enterprise (MOPE)
a5155.name: Wondafrash Assefa
a5155.title: Public Relation Head of the Ministry of Public Enterprise (MOPE)
a5155.speech: Said Lominat has beat out two other bidders: “Lominat offered the highest price, but others tabled a huge amount compared with the roof price that MOPE set.” ; He said that the other companies that participated on the bid are Pure Alcohol and Beverages Manufacturing and Metadim Manufacturing, with Pure proposing close to 1.7 billion birr and Metadim just over 1.5 billion birr.

a5155.speaker: Ministry of Public Enterprise (MOPE)
a5155.name: Ministry of Public Enterprise (MOPE)
a5155.speech: According to the information Capital obtained from MOPE, the initial price tagged on NALF was 1.27 billion birr.

a5155.speaker: Brook Worku, CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.name: Brook Worku
a5155.title: CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.speech: Told Capital that the company is worth what his company offered. “To be frank the company is one of the most profitable public enterprises, and has a huge market in the country.”

a5155.speaker: Brook Worku, CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.name: Brook Worku
a5155.title: CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.speech: “Me and Benyam, owner of Country Trading, created this partnership since he has ample experience in local distribution and trading alcohol and sprits, and I have wide relationships with multinational producers.”

a5155.speaker: Brook Worku, CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.name: Brook Worku
a5155.title: CEO of Lominat Beverages Plc
a5155.speech: “Our main aim is to develop the local market as per the international standard and completely substitute imports and even supply exports to the international market at an affordable price.” ; “We can produce the alcohol products and different brands that are imported from abroad and substitute exports by 90 percent.” ; “We have included the entire business plan in the bid.”

a5339.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Report and Accounts for the Year Ended December 31 2024
a5339.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM) Report and Accounts for the Year Ended December 31 2024
a5339.speech: Shows that tea output increased by 0.8 percent to 46.3 million kg in 2024, but the sector was affected by continued decline in prices. Reads the report in part: "Similarly, the volume of tea sold saw a marginal growth of 1.5 percent, reaching 5.5 million kilogrammes compared to 5.4 million kilogrammes in the previous year. However, tea prices dropped by 5.3 percent and averaged $1.23 [about K2 153] per kilogramme in 2024 from an average of $1.30 [about K2 276] per kilogramme in the preceding year. Consequently, tea sales proceeds declined to $6.8 million [about K11.9 billion] in 2024 from $7 million [about K12.3 billion] generated in 2023."

a5339.speaker: Tonda Chinangwa, Tea Association of Malawi Limited chief executive officer
a5339.name: Tonda Chinangwa
a5339.title: Tea Association of Malawi Limited chief executive officer
a5339.speech: Attributing the increased production to favourable weather conditions, said the quoted earnings are based on auction prices, which are way below export earnings after value-addition ; "In 2023, total tea production was 43.3 million kg and in 2024, total tea production increased to 49.7 million kg. The increase in tea production was due to favourable weather conditions, especially good rainfall. In 2023, total tea exports were 42.5 million kg with value of over K73.4 billion while in 2024, total tea exports were 41.7 million kg with K111 billion." ; said the prices were from direct auction prices, excluding the real export value after value-addition through blending, among others: "The real export earnings would, therefore, exceed the above estimated values."

a5339.speaker: Beatrice Makwenda, Trust Africa programme officer
a5339.name: Beatrice Makwenda
a5339.title: Trust Africa programme officer
a5339.speech: Attributed the improved production to current efforts to strengthen smallholder institutions ; "The tea sector is decisively working towards improving both production and productivity by strengthening smallholder institutions and creating a conducive environment for social dialogue. In 2021, the tea sector welcomed a partnership under Reclaim Sustainability Programme, which has supported the sector to engage with government for support towards production, market and advancing decent work." ; said the changes in industry practice coupled with research programmes targeting modern varieties and technologies, will result in ethical tea production, which will sustain current markets and open new opportunities.

a5339.speaker: Sangwani Hara, Tea Association chairperson
a5339.name: Sangwani Hara
a5339.title: Tea Association chairperson
a5339.speech: Told a tea testing event in London, United Kingdom last year that enhanced trade can provide a good alternative to aid and development assistance through increased exports of products like tea ; "With increased tea imports from Malawi, British tea drinkers will be allowed to consume a great product at a fair price while contributing to Malawi's and tea estates' foreign exchange earnings and development agenda."

a5361.speaker: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.name: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario
a5361.title: Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.speech: Urged the population of the northern province of Niassa not to allow themselves to be enticed by the terrorist groups operating in the neighbouring province of Cabo Delgado; told the displaced people that the government has not yet discovered what motivates the terrorist attacks; added that the terrorists behead their victims and destroy hospitals and schools and recruit by offering money to youths and to adults, and insisted such bribes should be rejected. “When a young man receives a bribe, he should say no” ; “He should say ‘Mozambique comes first. I cannot accept this enticement to go around cutting the throats of blameless people’” ; said all citizens should refuse to be recruited to destroy infrastructures such as bridges, schools and hospitals, “which are needed to improve the living conditions of Mozambican citizens” ; said the attitude of people offered bribes should be “I cannot receive money to destroy a bridge we need. I cannot receive money to destroy the place where my mother goes, or where I go myself when I am ill. I cannot receive money to destroy the place where children study so that tomorrow they can have the knowledge to develop Mozambique”.

a5361.speaker: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.name: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario
a5361.title: Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.speech: Recommended greater vigilance in order to neutralise rapidly any terrorist attempt to infiltrate Niassa.

a5361.speaker: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.name: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario
a5361.title: Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.speech: Announced that, in order to avoid Niassa youths falling into temptation, the government has drawn up job creation programmes that should be implemented as from next year.

a5361.speaker: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario, Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.name: Carlos Agostinho do Rosario
a5361.title: Mozambican Prime Minister
a5361.speech: Said the government is also committed to supporting displaced people currently living in the accommodation centres: “We shall provide support in food and in medical care, with the nurse we have here” ; “But we must create conditions so that we ourselves can produce our own food” ; promised that the government will grant land to the displaced where they can build new homes, as well as seeds so that they can produce food and guarantee their own sustenance.

a5385.speaker: Hussein Abdelbagi, Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of South Sudan
a5385.name: Hussein Abdelbagi
a5385.title: Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of South Sudan
a5385.speech: has called on the private sector to invest their resources and efforts in productive agricultural activities to boost the nation’s economy ; emphasized that the agriculture sector should be central to the country’s economic transformation ; pointed out that South Sudan is facing a critical juncture due to reductions in foreign aid, highlighting the urgent need for sustainable economic growth ; encouraged the private sector to draw lessons from countries like Kenya and Rwanda ; “South Sudan possesses vast arable land, rich water bodies, and a capable youth population. But, unless we put these to work, they will remain untapped potential” ; “Agriculture must become a cornerstone of economic transformation for subsistence to surplus and from fragmentation to commercialization.” ; “We call our the private sector to redirect their capital and energy toward productive agricultural ventures in farming through agriculture processing, value chain, irrigation, mechanization, storage, and export logistics” ; reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating a favorable environment for agri-businesses to thrive.

a5385.speaker: Farmers across South Sudan
a5385.name: Farmers across South Sudan
a5385.speech: have consistently raised concerns about the impact of conflict, insufficient government support, particularly regarding pest control, limited access to fuel, and the absence of stable markets for their agricultural products.

a5385.speaker: Lily Albino Akol, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of South Sudan
a5385.name: Lily Albino Akol
a5385.title: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security of South Sudan
a5385.speech: instructed all state governors and chief administrators to allocate 250,000 hectares of land in their respective states for agricultural purposes.

a5388.speaker: Mark Toner, US Ambassador to Liberia
a5388.name: Mark Toner
a5388.title: US Ambassador to Liberia
a5388.speech: “The effort is designed to enhance the skills of teachers to provide quality and inclusive education for students. The initiative is also aimed at addressing Education Minister Jarso Jallah’s vision to support academic and nutritional needs of school going children.” ; said the US Government is also proud to be a major contributor to global partnership in education.

a5388.speaker: Jarso Jallah, Liberian Education Minister
a5388.name: Jarso Jallah
a5388.title: Liberian Education Minister
a5388.speech: has praised the US Government through USAID for the unwavering support towards the Liberian Education System ; “The initiative will set the stage for a new era of learning, where every child will access resources, support and opportunities needed to succeed.” ; said investment in teachers means direct investment in the future of Liberia ; recognized local and international stakeholders for their dedication and commitment to the advancement of education.

a5530.speaker: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.name: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.speech: Has warned Nigerian travellers against the misuse of US visas; urged Nigerians to adhere to the travel purpose identified in their visa application, noting that violations will likely result in visa revocation or deportation, and said breaching visa conditions could also attract severe penalties, such as permanent removal from the US and ineligibility for future travel: “All visa holders are advised to adhere to the purpose stated in their visa applications strictly.” ; “Applicants are reminded that security screening by US authorities continues beyond initial entry. Any violation of immigration or other laws may result in visa revocation or deportation.”

a5530.speaker: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.name: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.speech: Asked Nigerian students in the US to remain in active study, noting that students who withdraw from schools, are perpetually absent or change academic programmes without notification are also likely to have their visas cancelled and might also lose future eligibility; added that consular officers may deny tourist visas if there is reason to believe the applicant’s primary intent is to give birth in the US and obtain citizenship for the child.

a5530.speaker: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.name: Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) (travel advisory/statement)
a5530.speech: “The NIS continues to collaborate with the US Mission in Abuja to ensure Nigeria is not included in any expanded visa restrictions.” ; “Compliance with visa regulations is essential to safeguard legitimate travel by Nigerian citizens.”

a5530.speaker: US Mission in Abuja / US Embassy (Facebook post)
a5530.name: US Mission in Abuja / US Embassy (Facebook post)
a5530.speech: Earlier warned that travelling to the US with the intent of giving birth would lead to sanctions, stating that requesting a visa with the sole aim of giving birth in the United States is not permitted and that consular officers will deny visa applications if they have reason to believe that this is the applicant’s intent: “Using your visa to travel for the primary purpose of giving birth in the United States so that your child will have US citizenship is not permitted.” ; “Consular officers will deny your visa application if they have reason to believe this is your intent.”

a5557.speaker: Official sources from the Chinese government
a5557.name: Official sources from the Chinese government
a5557.speech: Say the Chinese Foreign Minister, Wang Yi, will be visiting African countries from the 5th to the 11th of January, visiting four African countries, including Namibia, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Nigeria.

a5557.speaker: Xi Jinping, President of China
a5557.name: Xi Jinping
a5557.title: President of China
a5557.speech: Promised elevated strategic relationships between China and all African countries ; in 2024 pledged additional funding of $51 billion, including $10 billion in development assistance to support African projects in infrastructure, agriculture, industry, trade and investment.

a5557.speaker: Bola Ahmed Tinubu, President of Nigeria, and Xi Jinping, President of China
a5557.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
a5557.title: President of Nigeria, and Xi Jinping, President of China
a5557.speech: Both leaders are committed to deepening mutual trust and they firmly support each other in promoting integrated development in infrastructure, energy, and minerals.

a5557.speaker: Critics
a5557.name: Critics
a5557.speech: Insist that China's renewed push is a debt-trap diplomacy designed to shove African countries into debt to gain leverage over them.

a5557.speaker: China (official position)
a5557.name: China (official position)
a5557.speech: Continues to promise to jointly promote modernisation in Africa through a just and equitable partnership that provides a win-win cooperation and common development with mutual respect and non-interference.

a5557.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5557.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a5557.speech: Estimates that between $130 billion and $170 billion is needed each year for infrastructure on the continent and that there is a gap of between $68 billion and $108 billion.

a5557.speaker: Uche Igwe, scholar and senior political economy analyst (author)
a5557.name: Uche Igwe
a5557.title: scholar and senior political economy analyst (author)
a5557.speech: Argues there is an urgent need for strategic calibration in the partnership, especially on the part of Africa, and that the proposal that Africa should begin to negotiate with China as a bloc with a collective vision and strategic approach should be considered by countries; in addition, investment in value chains should be sought.

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: Statement released on Sunday, June 9, 2025 confirming that Mr. Ofori-Atta will make himself available to the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) after his medical treatment and recovery are complete ; “Once Mr. Ofori-Atta completes his surgery and recovers, he will return to Ghana and appear before the OSP in person. We believe his rights will be upheld and that, in time, the truth will vindicate him before the entire nation.”

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: Described the move by the OSP as a “premeditated theatrical stunt” designed to publicly humiliate Mr. Ofori-Atta, whom they say has never evaded legal accountability ; “Any suggestions that Mr. Ofori-Atta is fleeing justice are baseless, out of character, and simply untrue.”

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: Said the former minister is scheduled to undergo surgery on June 13 at the Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota, following a confirmed cancer diagnosis from a biopsy conducted in March, and noted that he had formally informed the OSP of his medical condition and requested a video-recorded interview instead of a physical appearance—an offer they claim was rejected ; “We remain perplexed by the OSP’s refusal, over the past three months, to accept Mr. Ofori-Atta’s proposal to provide information through written submissions or a recorded video interview. It is difficult to see this refusal as anything other than an attempt to embarrass him upon his return.”

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: Accused the Special Prosecutor’s office of manipulating evidence, violating Mr. Ofori-Atta’s constitutional rights, and ignoring pending legal proceedings, referencing a Human Rights Court ruling scheduled for June 18 and arguing that the arrest warrant was obtained without proper judicial process ; “There is no formal charge against Mr. Ofori-Atta apart from a vague reference in the arrest warrant to ‘using public office for private profit’. This warrant was issued under highly unusual circumstances and without a supporting affidavit.”

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: “We, the family of Mr. Kenneth Ofori-Atta, have chosen to make this public statement due to the actions of the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) on 2 June. We also call for the withdrawal of the INTERPOL Red Notice and have applied to the National Central Bureau and the Commission for the Control of INTERPOL’s Files for deletion of the Red Notice” — arguing the notice was issued without due consideration of his health condition, the pending court ruling, or his repeated offers of virtual cooperation.

a5575.speaker: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.name: Family of Ken Ofori-Atta (statement)
a5575.speech: Highlighted Mr. Ofori-Atta’s history of transparency, citing previous investigations by Parliament, the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ), and the ECOWAS Court, all of which reportedly cleared him of wrongdoing.

a5598.speaker: Emmanuel Cherem, 25-year-old gay man in Nigeria living with HIV
a5598.name: Emmanuel Cherem
a5598.title: 25-year-old gay man in Nigeria living with HIV
a5598.speech: Admits he should have been more careful about practicing safe sex but had become accustomed to using the U.S.-supplied pharmaceutical ; "I blame myself... Taking care of myself is my first duty as a person" ; "I equally blame the Trump administration because, you know, these things were available, and then, without prior notice, these things were cut off."

a5598.speaker: PrEPWatch, global tracker
a5598.name: PrEPWatch
a5598.title: global tracker
a5598.speech: According to PrEPWatch, the number of initiations, or people who have taken at least one dose of the drug, rose in Africa from fewer than 700 in 2016 to more than 6 million by late 2024; more than 90% of new initiations last year were financed by PEPFAR, using cheap generic versions of the drug.

a5598.speaker: UNAIDS, the United Nations AIDS agency
a5598.name: UNAIDS
a5598.title: the United Nations AIDS agency
a5598.speech: According to UNAIDS, sub-Saharan Africa had 390,000 AIDS-related deaths in 2023, or 62% of the global total.

a5598.speaker: World Health Organization
a5598.name: World Health Organization
a5598.speech: According to the WHO, that death toll was down by 56% from 2010.

a5598.speaker: UNAIDS fact sheet from May
a5598.name: UNAIDS fact sheet from May
a5598.speech: Restrictions on PrEP have coincided with dwindling supplies of more widely used HIV prevention tools like condoms and lubricants "because of the US funding cuts".

a5598.speaker: Nine activists and three medical experts
a5598.name: Nine activists and three medical experts
a5598.speech: Described the combination as a major threat to prevention across the continent.

a5598.speaker: Linda-Gail Bekker, HIV expert at the University of Cape Town
a5598.name: Linda-Gail Bekker
a5598.title: HIV expert at the University of Cape Town
a5598.speech: "I just see this as incredibly short-sighted because we were on a winning path" ; said that many African governments did not have the resources to spend on PrEP drugs on top of treatment for HIV infections, risking a worsening of the pandemic ; "It's as predictable as if you take your eye off a smouldering bushfire and the wind is blowing: a bushfire will come back."

a5598.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a5598.name: Donald Trump
a5598.title: U.S. President
a5598.speech: Has said that the United States pays disproportionately for foreign aid and he wants other countries to shoulder more of the burden, as he seeks to reduce U.S. government spending across the board.

a5598.speaker: Max Primorac, former senior USAID official, senior research fellow at The Heritage Foundation's Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom
a5598.name: Max Primorac
a5598.title: former senior USAID official, senior research fellow at The Heritage Foundation's Margaret Thatcher Center for Freedom
a5598.speech: "It's a question of who has primary responsibility for the health needs of citizens of other countries, and it's their own governments" ; "We all know, and this is a bipartisan issue, that aid dependency doesn't help these people - that the best solution is for these countries to be able to take over the responsibility of these programs."

a5598.speaker: UNAIDS
a5598.name: UNAIDS
a5598.speech: Says the permanent discontinuation of PEPFAR-supported prevention and treatment programs could lead to an additional 2,300 new HIV cases globally per day.

a5598.speaker: 23 health workers, PrEP users and activists interviewed by Reuters
a5598.name: 23 health workers
a5598.title: PrEP users and activists interviewed by Reuters
a5598.speech: Nearly all said that the increase in HIV infections since the funding cuts was impossible to quantify because many organisations working with vulnerable populations have been defunded.

a5598.speaker: Spokesperson for the U.S. State Department
a5598.name: Spokesperson for the U.S. State Department
a5598.speech: Told Reuters the department "continues to support lifesaving HIV testing, care and treatment, and prevention of mother to child transmission services approved by the Secretary of State" ; "All other PEPFAR-funded services are being reviewed for assessment of programmatic efficiencies and consistency with United States foreign policy" ; the spokesperson did not directly respond to a question about why the waiver had excluded vulnerable groups from PrEP distribution.

a5598.speaker: UNAIDS
a5598.name: UNAIDS
a5598.speech: Said in March that in East and Southern Africa, the sub-region accounting for more than half of all people living with HIV, the U.S. had been funding nearly 45% of HIV prevention programming, and that some countries like Malawi, Zimbabwe and Mozambique were almost entirely dependent on PEPFAR for their HIV prevention programs, while in wealthier nations like South Africa and Kenya PEPFAR represented less than 25% of spending on HIV prevention.

a5598.speaker: Russell Vought, director of the U.S. Office of Management and Budget
a5598.name: Russell Vought
a5598.title: director of the U.S. Office of Management and Budget
a5598.speech: Told a Congressional committee on June 4 that, due to high U.S. debt levels, Africa needed to shoulder more of the burden in fighting AIDS ; asked specifically about restrictions on HIV prevention programs, said: "We believe that many of these nonprofits are not geared toward the viewpoints of the administration."

a5598.speaker: Rachel Cauley, communications director for Russell Vought
a5598.name: Rachel Cauley
a5598.title: communications director for Russell Vought
a5598.speech: Said Trump "ran on ending woke and weaponized government," citing programs focused on climate and transgender rights issues.

a5598.speaker: Festus Alex Chinaza, executive director of Hearty Empowerment and Rights (HER) Initiative
a5598.name: Festus Alex Chinaza
a5598.title: executive director of Hearty Empowerment and Rights (HER) Initiative
a5598.speech: Said the organisation worked with other groups that provide HIV/AIDS services to confirm the men's diagnosis and help secure treatment for them.

a5598.speaker: Echezona, 30-year-old gay man in Asaba, Nigeria (first name only)
a5598.name: Echezona
a5598.title: 30-year-old gay man in Asaba, Nigeria (first name only)
a5598.speech: "I just pray and wish that Trump actually changes his policy and everything comes back to normal so that the spread and transmission of the virus would be reduced" ; described being told by staff at community-based clinics that PrEP was only available to pregnant and lactating women, in line with the Trump administration guidelines.

a5598.speaker: UNAIDS
a5598.name: UNAIDS
a5598.speech: According to UNAIDS, Nigeria has an adult HIV prevalence rate of 1.3% and an estimated 2 million people living with HIV, the fourth-highest total globally; South Africa has an estimated 7.7 million people living with HIV, the highest number in the world.

a5598.speaker: Survey completed in 2021
a5598.name: Survey completed in 2021
a5598.speech: According to the survey, rates for so-called key populations are much higher: 25% for men who have sex with men.

a5598.speaker: Nigerian health ministry
a5598.name: Nigerian health ministry
a5598.speech: Did not respond to a request for comment on the effects of the Trump administration's cuts to HIV prevention services.

a5598.speaker: Nine activists
a5598.name: Nine activists
a5598.speech: Said gay men and sex workers often avoid public health facilities where PrEP is free, fearing discrimination and harassment.

a5598.speaker: Francois Venter, executive director of the Ezintsha medical research center at the University of the Witwatersrand
a5598.name: Francois Venter
a5598.title: executive director of the Ezintsha medical research center at the University of the Witwatersrand
a5598.speech: Said PrEP distribution from public sector clinics in Johannesburg had shown almost no increase since the Trump cuts.

a5598.speaker: Foster Mohale, spokesperson for South Africa's health ministry
a5598.name: Foster Mohale
a5598.title: spokesperson for South Africa's health ministry
a5598.speech: Said the ministry was "not aware" of reports that key populations were avoiding health facilities due to stigma ; "We have sensitized health officials across the country to create (a) conducive environment for all healthcare seekers/clients to access the service without feeling judged or discriminated against."

a5744.speaker: Executive Mansion (press release dated August 15, 2025)
a5744.name: Executive Mansion (press release dated August 15
a5744.speech: According to the release, President Boakai is set to participate in the TICAD-9. He will be accompanied by a delegation comprising 23 members.

a5744.speaker: Analysts / critics
a5744.name: Analysts / critics
a5744.speech: Analysts have expressed significant concerns over the President's compliance with the Government of Liberia's Revised Travel Ordinance Law of 2025, which came into effect on January 2, 2025; critics argue that the President's delegation infringes on Rule #3.

a5744.speaker: Government of Liberia Revised Travel Ordinance Law of 2025 (document)
a5744.name: Government of Liberia Revised Travel Ordinance Law of 2025 (document)
a5744.speech: Rule #3 stipulates that "Total Government of Liberia-funded representation at any program or event held outside Liberia shall not exceed five (5) persons in total, regardless of how many entities are involved." Additionally, Rule #4 states that for specific high-level meetings, such as the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA), Africa-China Summit, Korea-Africa Summit, and the Commission on the Status of Women Conference, the maximum allowable number of delegates is capped at seven (7); the Daily Subsistence Allowance (DSA) for officials traveling abroad is established at US$344 daily, broken down into US$110 for meals and US$234 for hotel accommodations.

a5744.speaker: Coalition of civil society organizations, including prominent advocacy groups and community leaders (joint communique, June 2025)
a5744.name: Coalition of civil society organizations
a5744.title: including prominent advocacy groups and community leaders (joint communique, June 2025)
a5744.speech: Released a powerful joint communique urging the Liberian government to reject any austerity measures that could exacerbate the already critical economic situation. They emphasized the need for a fair and inclusive approach to debt restructuring and called for comprehensive reforms in the tax policies, which they argue disproportionately favor large corporations while imposing a heavier burden on ordinary citizens.

a5744.speaker: Boakai administration
a5744.name: Boakai administration
a5744.speech: Persistently urges the populace to display patience with the ARREST Agenda - an initiative designed to address critical sectors such as Agriculture, Roads, Rule of Law, Education, Sanitation, and Tourism; may assert that it prioritizes the well-being of its citizens.

a5747.speaker: Idi Maiha, Nigerian Livestock Minister
a5747.name: Idi Maiha
a5747.title: Nigerian Livestock Minister
a5747.speech: Said on Monday that Nigeria is importing dairy cattle from Denmark as it aims to double its milk output within five years, part of a plan to cut dairy imports that cost the country $1.5 billion a year: "Our goal is ambitious but achievable; to double Nigeria's milk production from 700,000 tonnes to 1.4 million tonnes annually in the next five years" ; "With over 20.9 million cattle, 60 million sheep, and 1.4 million goats already, we are not starting from zero, we are building from strength."

a5747.speaker: Idi Maiha, Nigerian Livestock Minister
a5747.name: Idi Maiha
a5747.title: Nigerian Livestock Minister
a5747.speech: Said Nigeria's cattle population, exceeding 20 million, consists largely of low-yield pastoralist breeds; said a Nigerian farm has already imported over 200 heifers from Denmark, building its herd through intensive breeding; said eight new pasture species have been registered, the first in 48 years, and a national strategy for animal genetic resources with support from the Food and Agriculture Organization has been launched.

a6198.speaker: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) initiative
a6198.name: IPC (Integrated Food Security Phase Classification) initiative
a6198.speech: According to the IPC initiative, which tracks extreme hunger globally, over 24.6 million people – half of Sudan’s population – are experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity.

a6198.speaker: IPC’s Famine Review Committee (FRC)
a6198.name: IPC’s Famine Review Committee (FRC)
a6198.speech: Confirmed that famine (IPC phase 5) is present in at least five areas, including North Darfur’s Zamzam camp and parts of the Western Nuba Mountains; the crisis is projected to expand further, with five additional areas – the North Darfur localities of Um Kadadah, Melit, El Fasher, At Tawisha, and Al Lait – expected to face famine between December 2024 and May 2025, and 17 other areas at risk of famine.

a6198.speaker: IPC report
a6198.name: IPC report
a6198.speech: “Famine is the most extreme manifestation of human suffering, representing a catastrophic collapse of the systems and resources essential for survival.” ; “It is not merely a lack of food but a profound breakdown of health, livelihoods, and social structures, leaving entire communities in a state of desperation.”

a6198.speaker: IPC report
a6198.name: IPC report
a6198.speech: According to the report, farmers were forced to abandon fields, and crops were looted or destroyed, with displaced families remaining cut off from the benefits of the harvest; 8.1 million people are classified in IPC phase 4 (emergency) and 638,000 are already in phase 5 (catastrophe), adding to 15.9 million in phase 3 (crisis).

a6198.speaker: IPC report
a6198.name: IPC report
a6198.speech: Underscored that only an immediate cessation of hostilities can prevent the crisis from worsening; called for the restoration of safe, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access, particularly in conflict zones, and a significant scale-up of multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance; and also called for scaling up treatment for acute malnutrition, providing vital agricultural inputs, and conducting food security and nutrition surveys in unassessed areas.

a6419.speaker: Abdoul Karim Diarra, National Director of Human Rights of Mali
a6419.name: Abdoul Karim Diarra
a6419.title: National Director of Human Rights of Mali
a6419.speech: Said the "Human Rights Cafe" is intended to be a space for exchange and awareness-raising between experts and the Malian citizen, held periodically to promote constructive dialogue between institutions and the population on human rights, as a monthly meeting in Bamako or in certain regions of Mali, supported and financed by USAID through its "Sariya-Bato" project ; "This Human Rights Cafe aims to improve the population's understanding of human rights by addressing essential themes," citing among others "women's rights, the fight against slavery, human trafficking, children's rights, respect for human rights in the fight against terrorism, transnational organised crime, cybercrime, and respect for human rights in places of deprivation of liberty."

a6419.speaker: Mamoudou Kassogue, Minister of Justice and Human Rights of Mali, former prosecutor of the Anti-Corruption Unit
a6419.name: Mamoudou Kassogue
a6419.title: Minister of Justice and Human Rights of Mali, former prosecutor of the Anti-Corruption Unit
a6419.speech: Dissected corruption in its many aspects, fields and sectors in Mali: "Corruption must be banished in Mali. A corrupt state is a bankrupt state." He cited several cases of corruption and their consequences for the fundamental rights of human beings in Mali.

a6419.speaker: Richard Kimball, Deputy Director of USAID-Mali
a6419.name: Richard Kimball
a6419.title: Deputy Director of USAID-Mali
a6419.speech: Said the Sariya-Bato project ("Respect for the law") is financed by USAID over a period of 5 years and aims to support the efforts of the Ministry of Justice and Human Rights; for him, the presence of the Minister of Justice as a speaker at this Human Rights Cafe demonstrates the importance the department attaches to the question of human rights.

a6429.speaker: Concorde Nsengumuremyi, Director General of Rwanda Forestry Authority
a6429.name: Concorde Nsengumuremyi
a6429.title: Director General of Rwanda Forestry Authority
a6429.speech: "The trees will be planted under 2023/24 tree planting season from October up to early December this year," adding that indigenous trees have the potential for the country's carbon market, in line with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement signed in 2015 ; He said the country will plant 4.9 million fruit trees, 6.7 million ornamental trees, 273,590 bamboo trees, 34.2 million agro-forestry trees and 16.5 million trees in general for different uses, with 3.4 million and 2.2 million trees to be planted in Nyagatare and Rulindo districts respectively.

a6429.speaker: Experts
a6429.name: Experts
a6429.speech: Experts have said that carbon markets have the potential to be the next biggest export for the African continent, ensuring both environmental preservation and restoration while attracting substantive levels of fresh climate finance.

a6429.speaker: Herman Hakuzimana, Climate Change Programme Manager at the Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA)
a6429.name: Herman Hakuzimana
a6429.title: Climate Change Programme Manager at the Rwanda Environment Management Authority (REMA)
a6429.speech: Said the carbon market framework serves as a tool to attract investors to Rwanda's carbon market, and that these projects are all part of Rwanda's 10-year climate action plan, which requires $11 billion for implementation through 2030.

a6429.speaker: Rwanda's 10-year climate action plan (document)
a6429.name: Rwanda's 10-year climate action plan (document)
a6429.speech: The plan shows that new forests will be planted on 2,500 hectares; the plan aims to reduce an estimated total of 4.6 million tonnes of carbon emissions by 2030, a 38% decrease, through various interventions including in the forestry sector.

a6429.speaker: Charles Sindayigaya, project Coordinator
a6429.name: Charles Sindayigaya
a6429.title: project Coordinator
a6429.speech: According to him, radical and progressive terraces and afforestation activities will also improve agricultural productivity and restore degraded ecosystems. "The stoves we are distributing will also contribute to achieving the project's goal of restoring the natural forests, as the stoves save energy compared to the traditional way of cooking."

a6602.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a6602.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a6602.speech: Reiterated the need to boost exports as a way of enhancing the country's foreign exchange reserves.

a6602.speaker: Boston Maliketi Banda, Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a6602.name: Boston Maliketi Banda
a6602.title: Reserve Bank of Malawi spokesperson
a6602.speech: Said in an interview that the country had managed on these levels of foreign reserves for decades ; said that to achieve Malawi's foreign exchange aspirations sustainably, there was a need to strengthen the capacity of export generation productive sectors ; “We are encouraged with the cooperation we are getting from [authorised dealer] banks in the country in supporting measures aimed at boosting foreign exchange reserves. Looking ahead, this cooperation should result in a thriving private sector that exports its products and generates foreign exchange, which is vital for stabilising the foreign exchange market and maintaining price stability.”

a6602.speaker: Marvin Banda, economic expert
a6602.name: Marvin Banda
a6602.title: economic expert
a6602.speech: Said in a recent interview that the country could not earn substantial forex when nearly all it exported were raw materials ; said it was baffling to see that even though the authorities had been trying to divert national productivity away from tobacco, a staggering proportion of total exports were owed to it.

a6602.speaker: Malawi Financial Market Update for the week ending February 28 2025, published by Bridgepath Capital Limited (report)
a6602.name: Malawi Financial Market Update for the week ending February 28 2025
a6602.title: published by Bridgepath Capital Limited (report)
a6602.speech: Shows that in January 2024, total reserves stood at $576.70 million (2.3 months of imports); in February the forex reserves took a slight dip to $540.32 million (2.2 months of imports), signalling early signs of economic pressure; reserves saw intermittent recovery and decline, with a peak in April reaching $603.07 million (2.4 months of imports); by October reserves had fallen to $519.0 million (2.1 months of imports) before a slight peak to $530.9 million (2.1 months of imports).

a6606.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, Deputy Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Account in charge of operations and implementation of compacts for Africa
a6606.name: Jonathan Bloom
a6606.title: Deputy Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Account in charge of operations and implementation of compacts for Africa
a6606.speech: Explained the implications of the decision and future prospects at a press conference, and reassured the people of Benin that the country can still win the second MCA compact ; said that this year, and for the first time, Benin had failed its corruption-control indicator: of the three criteria, it was on governance, with Justice, that Benin failed, passing five of six indicators.

a6606.speaker: Jonathan Bloom, Deputy Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Account
a6606.name: Jonathan Bloom
a6606.title: Deputy Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Account
a6606.speech: Said the major consequence is likely to be a delay of roughly six months to a year, so that at the earliest Benin could benefit from the second compact in 2015, with the Board due to meet in December 2014 to decide again on Benin's case; and that this would be an opportunity for Benin to strengthen its governance in the fight against corruption, notably by giving the National Anti-Corruption Authority resources ; said Benin still has the year 2014 to succeed on the corruption-control indicator.

a6606.speaker: Board of Directors of the MCC (Millennium Challenge Corporation)
a6606.name: Board of Directors of the MCC (Millennium Challenge Corporation)
a6606.speech: Decided not to place Benin among the first beneficiaries of the compact ; also decided to continue the formulation of the compact with Benin, in a somewhat limited way.

a6606.speaker: Coordination Unit for the Formulation (UCF) of the 2nd compact and monitoring of MCA-Benin reforms, coordinated by Samuel Batcho (press conference)
a6606.name: Coordination Unit for the Formulation (UCF) of the 2nd compact and monitoring of MCA-Benin reforms
a6606.title: coordinated by Samuel Batcho (press conference)
a6606.speech: Held a press conference in order to provide the Beninese people with credible information, from a reliable and independent source, on Benin's ineligibility for the second MCA compact.

a6612.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary-General
a6612.name: Antonio Guterres
a6612.title: UN Secretary-General
a6612.speech: Warns that the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are on the verge of becoming "the epitaph for a world that might have been."

a6612.speaker: ODI report (Kevin Watkins and co-authors)
a6612.name: ODI report (Kevin Watkins and co-authors)
a6612.speech: In a recent ODI report, my co-authors and I estimate that some 257 million children in IDA-eligible countries are growing up hungry, with devastating consequences for their health and educational prospects.

a6612.speaker: World Bank
a6612.name: World Bank
a6612.speech: Has rightly made the case for a major IDA increase.

a6612.speaker: Ajay Banga, World Bank President
a6612.name: Ajay Banga
a6612.title: World Bank President
a6612.speech: Last year called on donors to provide more than 120 billion dollars, which would make this replenishment "the biggest of all time."

a6612.speaker: David Lammy, UK Foreign Secretary
a6612.name: David Lammy
a6612.title: UK Foreign Secretary
a6612.speech: Has promised a new era in which the UK will "use realist means to pursue progressive ends."

a6612.speaker: UK Treasury
a6612.name: UK Treasury
a6612.speech: Wants to cap any additional contribution at 20pc and 40pc, and notes that it inherited a poisoned chalice of unsustainable public finance from its Conservative predecessors, suggesting that the UK cannot afford to send a positive signal in the interest of international cooperation and its soft power.

a6653.speaker: Rodrigue Alofa, customs inspector and head of the Borgou-Alibori regional anti-fraud service
a6653.name: Rodrigue Alofa
a6653.title: customs inspector and head of the Borgou-Alibori regional anti-fraud service
a6653.speech: According to him, the finding made after the operation carried out by a team of the criminal brigade, northern Parakou branch, was of 1,000 12-calibre Rio Buck Shot cartridges, 500 26-calibre Rio Game Load cartridges and 13,500 12-calibre Rio Redstar cartridges seized.

a6766.speaker: Mozambique government management plan (launched Thursday)
a6766.name: Mozambique government management plan (launched Thursday)
a6766.speech: According to the management plan launched on Thursday, Mozambique's government will use drones to prevent and monitor extreme weather events in the country.

a6766.speaker: Americo Muchanga, Mozambique's Minister of Telecommunications and Digital Transformation
a6766.name: Americo Muchanga
a6766.title: Mozambique's Minister of Telecommunications and Digital Transformation
a6766.speech: "The project marks an important step in transforming the way our country faces the challenges posed by extreme events of hydro-meteorological origin, which have caused major damage to our population and infrastructure" ; said using this technology to predict and manage the natural disasters that have struck the country will make obtaining accurate, real-time data on the affected areas easier, "preserving human lives" ; "The use of drones as tools for monitoring and mapping affected areas (...) is an innovative solution that promises to transform how we deal with these disasters" ; said the plan also includes training technicians from Mozambique's disaster management and climate areas to handle these devices.

a6766.speaker: Akposso Marcelle, African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6766.name: Akposso Marcelle
a6766.title: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6766.speech: Explained that, far beyond technological advances, this project represents a "clear commitment" to the safety of the population: "More than the introduction of technology, [the project aims] fundamentally to save lives, reduce the risk of disasters and improve Mozambique's response capacity."

a6766.speaker: Akposso Marcelle, African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6766.name: Akposso Marcelle
a6766.title: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a6766.speech: Added that the project will be implemented in six months after the drones are delivered in mid-May.

a6766.speaker: Luisa Meque, president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
a6766.name: Luisa Meque
a6766.title: president of the National Institute for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management
a6766.speech: Said the humanitarian assistance plan "defines actions to respond to internal displacement and poverty reduction in terms of access to basic social services such as education, health, sanitation and water supply, social inclusion and security, as well as economic protection and opportunities."

a6766.speaker: National Statistics Institute (data)
a6766.name: National Statistics Institute (data)
a6766.speech: According to data from the National Statistics Institute, extreme events such as cyclones and storms caused at least 1,016 deaths in Mozambique between 2019 and 2023, affecting around 4.9 million people.

a6766.speaker: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (data)
a6766.name: Africa Center for Strategic Studies (data)
a6766.speech: According to data from the Africa Center for Strategic Studies, an academic institution of the US Department of Defense that analyses conflicts in Africa, in 2024 alone at least 349 people died in attacks by Islamic extremist groups in Cabo Delgado province, an increase of 36%.

a6827.speaker: Luisa Meque, chairperson of the National Disaster Risk Management Institute (INGD)
a6827.name: Luisa Meque
a6827.title: chairperson of the National Disaster Risk Management Institute (INGD)
a6827.speech: Speaking on Sunday in Nampula city at a meeting of the Emergency Operational Committee aimed at assessing the impact of the cyclone, said at least 250,000 people may need humanitarian assistance as a result of the passage of Chido.

a6827.speaker: Northern Regional Water Board (ARA-Norte)
a6827.name: Northern Regional Water Board (ARA-Norte)
a6827.speech: According to ARA-Norte, the storm may also raise the level of the main rivers in the northern provinces; ARA-Norte called on communities to observe the relevant precautionary measures and avoid crossing watercourses.

a6882.speaker: Joseph Nyuma Boakai, President of Liberia
a6882.name: Joseph Nyuma Boakai
a6882.title: President of Liberia
a6882.speech: Congratulated the new volunteers and praised the U.S. Government for its continued support of Liberia: “This cohort marks another step in the enduring partnership between Liberia and the Peace Corps” ; “The Peace Corps is more than a program; it is a gift from the American people, offering knowledge, compassion, and solidarity to our communities.”

a6882.speaker: Mark C. Toner, outgoing U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a6882.name: Mark C. Toner
a6882.title: outgoing U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a6882.speech: Highlighted the long-standing impact of Peace Corps Volunteers in Liberia, noting that there are individuals who served 5, 10, 15, and even 30 years ago whose influence is still felt in the communities they supported: “Liberia continues to call them to service, and together, Returned Peace Corps Volunteers and communities all across Liberia continue to address unmet needs.”

a6882.speaker: Jarso Maley Jallah, Minister of Education (Liberia)
a6882.name: Jarso Maley Jallah
a6882.title: Minister of Education (Liberia)
a6882.speech: Thanked the Peace Corps for aligning its efforts with the Government’s ARREST Agenda, which he believes emphasizes quality, equity, and innovation in education, particularly in STEM, English, science subjects, and digital literacy.

a6882.speaker: Vernice Guthrie, Peace Corps Liberia Country Director
a6882.name: Vernice Guthrie
a6882.title: Peace Corps Liberia Country Director
a6882.speech: Applauded the collaboration between the Peace Corps, the Government, and local communities, recognizing the dedication of her staff and the training they provided in preparing the volunteers for their service.

a6999.speaker: Ministry of Health (MoH), Malawi
a6999.name: Ministry of Health (MoH)
a6999.title: Malawi
a6999.speech: Has admitted that the suspension of aid by the United States (US) government has put the health sector in a difficult position as some critical services have been closed, compromising public healthcare service delivery.

a6999.speaker: Matias Joshua, MoH Chief of Health Services
a6999.name: Matias Joshua
a6999.title: MoH Chief of Health Services
a6999.speech: Said in Lilongwe Thursday, at the launch of the Pen-Plus initiative by the World Health Organisation, that all US-funded laboratories were non-functional because they were being operated by US-recruited technicians that have been put on administrative leave ; said this closure comes following the delayed integration of the laboratories and other donor-funded services into the government system, stressing that crucial reforms to reduce dependence on foreign aid were a must now, regardless of the pain that would inevitably come ; said some reforms include scaling up paid-for services in public hospitals to reduce resource gaps and limit the effects of funding shocks ; “[The] time of relying on donor support is now elapsing. We need to strategise on how we move forward with our health services.”

a6999.speaker: National Health Financing Strategy 2023-2030 (Malawi)
a6999.name: National Health Financing Strategy 2023-2030 (Malawi)
a6999.speech: According to the strategy, the health system is heavily under-resourced, with per capita total health expenditure at an estimated $39.9, compared to the recommended public sources expenditure of $86 for low-income countries; much of the sector's financing is highly donor-dependent, with 54.5 percent of all resources coming from donors ; “Of all [the] resources, 40.3 percent are pooled under the government scheme. However, the percentage of resources managed by the government is slightly less, at 39.4 percent, indicating that the government has less control than donors in making direct expenditure decisions.”

a6999.speaker: Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo, WHO representative to Malawi
a6999.name: Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo
a6999.title: WHO representative to Malawi
a6999.speech: Declined to comment on the situation when asked about the impact of the aid freeze on foreign interventions in the country's health delivery systems.

a6999.speaker: Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo, WHO representative to Malawi
a6999.name: Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo
a6999.title: WHO representative to Malawi
a6999.speech: Has since urged all districts that are implementing the PEN-Plus initiative to make full use of additional resources to be provided for NCD services ; “This launch of Pen-Plus interventions in Machinga, Ntcheu, and Mchinji, as part of the national scale-up, does not undermine the government's efforts for integrated service delivery. It ensures the functionality of NCD services so that integrated service delivery under the Health Sector Strategic Plan 3 becomes a reality.”

a6999.speaker: Presentation at the Pen-Plus launch event (Machinga District data)
a6999.name: Presentation at the Pen-Plus launch event (Machinga District data)
a6999.speech: Showed that in Machinga District NCDs were claiming 65 percent of patients, out of the recorded cases under the Pen-Plus initiative.

a7050.speaker: Local experts and journalists interviewed for this report (anonymous)
a7050.name: Local experts and journalists interviewed for this report (anonymous)
a7050.speech: Interviewed in March 2023, June 2024 and May 2025, confirmed that the broadcaster remains effectively tethered to state interests, with limited room for dissenting or critical perspectives.

a7050.speaker: Imran Khan, then Prime Minister of Pakistan
a7050.name: Imran Khan
a7050.title: then Prime Minister of Pakistan
a7050.speech: Pledged in 2018 to roll back censorship across state media; however, this initiative failed to translate into tangible change.

a7050.speaker: Dragomir, M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC)
a7050.name: Dragomir
a7050.title: M. (2025), State Media Monitor Global Dataset 2025, Media and Journalism Research Center (MJRC)

a7082.speaker: Ian Chappell, former Australia captain (ESPNcricinfo column)
a7082.name: Ian Chappell
a7082.title: former Australia captain (ESPNcricinfo column)
a7082.speech: Wrote: “The ODI has been reduced to virtually depending on a World Cup year for its importance.”

a7082.speaker: Sachin Tendulkar, India great and 2011 World Cup winner
a7082.name: Sachin Tendulkar
a7082.title: India great and 2011 World Cup winner
a7082.speech: Believes the 50-over format is now too formulaic: “The game is becoming too predictable” ; “From the 15th to the 40 over, it's losing its momentum. It's getting boring.”

a7082.speaker: Mark Nicholas, incoming MCC president
a7082.name: Mark Nicholas
a7082.title: incoming MCC president
a7082.speech: Believes all other ODIs ought to be on the way out: “We believe strongly that ODIs should be World Cups only” ; “We think it's difficult bilaterally now to justify them. They're not filling grounds in a lot of countries. And there is a power at the moment to T20 cricket that is almost supernatural.” ; “In a free market, the most money wins. And that's just the end-game. The players can see that bubbling away and they want to be a part of it. So, it is an extraordinary power that T20 has, and I think scheduling 50-over cricket alongside it just continues the story of the death knell of the ODI game.”

a7124.speaker: Dr Geofrey Tarimo, THPS Regional Manager for Kigoma
a7124.name: Dr Geofrey Tarimo
a7124.title: THPS Regional Manager for Kigoma
a7124.speech: Revealed the news to journalists over the weekend in Kasulu that 37 infants born to HIV-positive mothers all tested negative, noting that this achievement is one of the major successes of the Afya Hatua project, which is being implemented in all nine councils of the region ; "PMTCT aims to prevent HIV transmission from HIV-positive mothers to their babies during pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding. All pregnant women attending Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) clinics are tested for HIV during their first visit. Those who test positive are immediately enrolled on antiretroviral therapy (ARVs) to prevent transmission."

a7124.speaker: Dr Geofrey Tarimo, THPS Regional Manager for Kigoma
a7124.name: Dr Geofrey Tarimo
a7124.title: THPS Regional Manager for Kigoma
a7124.speech: He thanked the government for its enabling policies that support the delivery of life-saving health services across the region.

a7124.speaker: Leticia Joseph, beneficiary at Kiganamo Health Centre
a7124.name: Leticia Joseph
a7124.title: beneficiary at Kiganamo Health Centre
a7124.speech: "I had lost hope, but that changed when I started receiving care at this centre. My baby was born healthy and HIV-free because of the quality services I received."

a7124.speaker: Rosemary Josephat, in-charge of the Kiganamo Health Centre CTC
a7124.name: Rosemary Josephat
a7124.title: in-charge of the Kiganamo Health Centre CTC
a7124.speech: Noted that the facility was established in December 2012 and currently serves 616 clients, including 163 men and 463 women, of whom 18 are pregnant and 76 are breastfeeding mothers.

a7124.speaker: Dr Hosea William, Kigoma Regional Coordinator for HIV/AIDS, STIs and Hepatitis
a7124.name: Dr Hosea William
a7124.title: Kigoma Regional Coordinator for HIV/AIDS, STIs and Hepatitis
a7124.speech: Said that Kigoma has the lowest HIV prevalence rate in Tanzania at 1.7 per cent, according to the 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey, down from 2.9 per cent in the 2016-2017 survey.

a7124.speaker: Dr Hosea William, Kigoma Regional Coordinator for HIV/AIDS, STIs and Hepatitis
a7124.name: Dr Hosea William
a7124.title: Kigoma Regional Coordinator for HIV/AIDS, STIs and Hepatitis
a7124.speech: "We are working closely with THPS in implementing HIV prevention, care and treatment services through regional and council health management teams (R/CHMTs). Currently, 283 health centres in the region provide PMTCT services and 94 Care and Treatment Centres (CTCs) operate in Kigoma, 74 of which are directly supported by the Afya Hatua project."

a7124.speaker: 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey
a7124.name: 2022-2023 Tanzania HIV Impact Survey
a7124.speech: Put Kigoma's HIV prevalence rate at 1.7 per cent, down from 2.9 per cent in the 2016-2017 survey.

a7235.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a7235.name: Filipe Nyusi
a7235.title: Mozambican President
a7235.speech: Believes that Saudi Arabia is a strategic and important partner for Africa, when it comes to diversification of African economies; speaking on Friday in Riyadh, during the first Saudi-Africa summit, said that with regard to the exploitation of natural resources, Saudi Arabia is one of the world's examples in promoting sustainable development: "The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia is one of the few countries where natural resources are not a curse, but are the driving force behind the development and well-being of its people. Africa can learn a lot from this reality" ; believes that Saudi Arabia's collaboration with African countries, especially in the areas of education, health and humanitarian assistance, may play a relevant role.

a7235.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a7235.name: Filipe Nyusi
a7235.title: Mozambican President
a7235.speech: "We reiterate our gratitude for the humanitarian assistance that the King Salman Humanitarian Support and Assistance Center has provided to Mozambique at a time when we are facing the severe consequences of the natural disasters that strike cyclically."

a7235.speaker: Filipe Nyusi, Mozambican President
a7235.name: Filipe Nyusi
a7235.title: Mozambican President
a7235.speech: "Let's try to achieve peace by all means," Nyusi declared, adding that the summit "is also an opportunity to confront the scourge of terrorism and violent extremism that affects our countries and undermines peace and political stability".
